content: By K. Gopalakrishnan With nearly three decades of experience and over 300 machines supplied worldwide, InspirOn Engineering continues to develop its Motex stenter range around energy efficiency, process control, fabric versatility and dependable after-sales support. Executive Director Mrs. Radhika Bhagwati discusses the company’s technological strengths, evolving customer requirements and plans for INDIA ITME 2026. InspirOn Engineering has steadily strengthened its position in textile finishing through its Motex range of stenter machines, combining engineering expertise with a focus on productivity, fabric quality and cost-effectiveness. The company’s journey in stenter manufacturing began in 1996 through a joint venture with A.Monforts, Germany. Since then, it has supplied more than 300 machines worldwide. Mrs. Radhika Bhagwati, Executive Director According to Mrs. Radhika Bhagwati, (ED), InspirOn Engineering, three priorities are increasingly shaping product development: sustainability, automation and flexibility. Textile processors require equipment that can handle diverse fabric types, deliver consistent quality and reduce energy consumption without compromising productivity. “Customers expect machines that save energy, handle diverse fabrics and deliver consistent quality , and that’s where Motex has evolved,” she says. Engineering for Productivity and Energy Efficiency A key differentiator of the Motex range is its patented Uniflo Air Circulation system, which delivers up to 15% higher drying efficiency at the same power consumption, according to the company. The stenters also incorporate a chamber-design heating system intended to optimise utility consumption. summary: The emergence of linear block silicone copolymers marked a major paradigm shift in textile finishing, overcoming the performance trade-offs inherent in conventional amino and amido-silicone softeners. By integrating alternating segments of flexible polydimethylsiloxane and amino blocks into a single backbone, this unique architecture maximizes luxurious hand-feel while radically enhancing yellowing resistance and application stability. Unlike […] The post Plug-and-play silicone softener provides effortless textile finishing appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: The emergence of linear block silicone copolymers marked a major paradigm shift in textile finishing, overcoming the performance trade-offs inherent in conventional amino and amido-silicone softeners. By integrating alternating segments of flexible polydimethylsiloxane and amino blocks into a single backbone, this unique architecture maximizes luxurious hand-feel while radically enhancing yellowing resistance and application stability. Unlike traditional silicones that frequently fail under harsh processing conditions, the securely configured functional groups in block silicones withstand high shear, extreme pH, and elevated temperatures. Figure: Edward Menezes, Executive Chairman, Rossari Biotech Ltd. While most standard block copolymers effectively use high-shear homogenization or microemulsification to form oil-in-water emulsions stabilized by suitable surfactants, this approach carries some inherent practical and technical limitations. Process dependency: Achieving and maintaining a fine, stable emulsion particle size depends on emulsification equipment, surfactant selection, and careful process control, both at the manufacturer and, for in-house emulsified products, at the mill. Bath stability issues: Conventional emulsions can be sensitive to electrolytes, hardness, pH swings, and the presence of other anionic or cationic auxiliaries in the finishing bath, increasing the risk of creaming, flocculation, or silicone spotting on fabric. Shelf-life and logistics: Coarser or less robustly stabilized emulsions are more prone to phase separation during storage and transport, particularly across temperature fluctuations. title: A Team: Building the Taiwan–India Bridge for Next-Generation Textiles
title_ko: A 팀: 차세대 섬유를 위한 대만-인도 가교 구축
summary: By K. Gopalakrishnan Jintex’s Ganesh H.R. explains how A Team is combining Taiwanese machinery, chemistry, automation and process expertise to help Indian manufacturers accelerate their move into MMF, sportswear and… The post A Team: Building the Taiwan–India Bridge for Next-Generation Textiles appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: By K. Gopalakrishnan Jintex’s Ganesh H.R. explains how A Team is combining Taiwanese machinery, chemistry, automation and process expertise to help Indian manufacturers accelerate their move into MMF, sportswear and technical textiles. India’s textile industry is entering a decisive new phase. The country has built formidable scale and capability in cotton, but the next wave of growth is increasingly being shaped by man-made fibres (MMF), functional textiles, sportswear, athleisure and technical applications. Recognising this shift, Jintex Corporation Ltd. has joined forces with a group of established Taiwanese machinery, automation and textile-technology companies to create A Team—an integrated platform designed to bring Taiwan’s synthetic-textile know-how closer to Indian manufacturers. In an interaction with The Textile Magazine, Ganesh H.R., Senior Vice President – South Asia, Jintex Corporation Ltd., explains why India’s synthetic-textile opportunity is gathering momentum, how A Team was conceived, and why technology must be supported by process knowledge, local service and application expertise if India is to compete successfully in global performance-textile markets. Ganesh H.R., Senior Vice President – South Asia, Jintex Corporation Ltd. India’s Synthetic Opportunity India’s shift towards synthetics has become far more visible over the past three to four years. Jintex had been tracking the segment for more than a decade, but Ganesh says the recent acceleration is materially different in both pace and intent. The structural reason is clear: while India remains strongly cotton-oriented, the global fibre mix is increasingly dominated by synthetics. summary: Fong’s National Engineering Co. Ltd. and Pacific Global Associates Ltd. (PGAL) jointly organized Fong’s Open Day 2026 at Rahim Textile Mills Ltd. – a concern of Knit Asia Limited (Unit-2) in Shafipur,...
content: Fong’s National Engineering Co. Ltd. and Pacific Global Associates Ltd. (PGAL) jointly organized Fong’s Open Day 2026 at Rahim Textile Mills Ltd. – a concern of Knit Asia Limited (Unit-2) in Shafipur, Gazipur, bringing textile dyeing professionals closer to the latest developments in dyeing machinery, process control and after-sales support. Figure 1: Textile dyeing professionals in the Fong’s Open Day 2026 event. The event centered on the Fong’s Softwin Dyeing Machine, the latest model introduced to the Bangladesh market through the collaboration between Fong’s and Pacific Global. Industry professionals attending the open day had the opportunity to observe the machine in an operating factory environment and learn about its application for demanding knitted fabrics. Softwin has been developed particularly for heavy-GSM and compact fabrics, where crease marks and related fabric-quality problems can become a major challenge during dyeing. Speaking at the event, Mohammad Rafed Hossain Nobel, Director, Pacific Global Associates Ltd., said Pacific Global has been supplying Fong’s dyeing machinery and providing sales and technical support in Bangladesh for many years. He explained that the Softwin machine has been introduced to address one of the recurring concerns of dye houses handling heavier and tighter fabric structures. Figure 2: Mohammad Rafed Hossain Nobel, Director, Pacific Global Associates Ltd. “Many of our customers face crease-mark problems, particularly when processing high-GSM and compact fabrics. With this machine, several customers have been able to overcome those problems and are operating it satisfactorily,” he said. summary: New textile finishing technologies introduced by Switzerland’s Sanitized and Germany’s Rudolf are designed to address two factors that can limit the useful life of clothing and technical textiles – persistent odours and declining weather protection. Sanitized has introduced Odorex EON, a biocide-free treatment developed to tackle the accumulation of body oils and odour-causing residues in […] The post Helping fabrics retain their functional properties appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: New textile finishing technologies introduced by Switzerland’s Sanitized and Germany’s Rudolf are designed to address two factors that can limit the useful life of clothing and technical textiles – persistent odours and declining weather protection. Sanitized has introduced Odorex EON, a biocide-free treatment developed to tackle the accumulation of body oils and odour-causing residues in performance apparel, while Rudolf has launched Ruco-Dry Eco CWS, a water-repellent finish designed to provide improved resistance to rain and moisture, particularly in cotton fabrics. The two companies are highlighting their respective developments as part of a broader approach to textile durability that extends beyond conventional measures such as strength, abrasion resistance and wash performance. One particular challenge for sportswear manufacturers is the persistence of unpleasant odours in synthetic garments, even after repeated laundering. Sometimes referred to as “permastink”, this can result from the gradual accumulation of sebum and other residues within textile fibres. Sanitized Odorex EON employs a dual-action approach intended to address both immediate odours and their longer-term accumulation. During wear, the treatment adsorbs and neutralises odour molecules, while also creating a protective layer that helps release sebum residues during laundering. The aim is to prevent the progressive build-up of contaminants that can make otherwise serviceable garments unpleasant to wear. content: Techtextil and Texprocess will return to Frankfurt am Main from 4-7 April 2028 with a stronger focus on connecting materials, production technologies and textile processing. The two international trade fairs will introduce an optimised hall layout designed to encourage collaboration, improve visitor navigation and generate new business opportunities across the textile value chain. Against a backdrop of volatile markets, rising costs and changing global supply chains, the events aim to help textile manufacturers, technology suppliers and end users identify new partnerships and applications. Developments in advanced materials, automation and artificial intelligence are creating opportunities for innovation, making closer cooperation between different stages of production increasingly important. Organiser Messe Frankfurt says the concurrent staging of Techtextil and Texprocess provides a significant advantage by bringing together research organisations, material suppliers, machinery manufacturers, processors and industrial users at a single location. The close relationship between the two events was evident in 2026, when 87% of Texprocess trade visitors also attended Techtextil, while 68% of Techtextil visitors explored Texprocess. Around 80% of exhibitors reported achieving their trade fair objectives. Several leading international companies have already confirmed their participation in the 2028 editions. Early registrations for Techtextil include Angles Textil/Antex, Beaulieu Fibres International, CHT, Dilo Systems, Getzner Textil, Huvis Corporation, Lenzing, Sioen Industries and Toray Textiles Europe. title: New garment wage structure to take effect in December
summary: A revised wage structure for Bangladesh’s garment workers will come into effect in December, according to members of the newly formed wage board. Representatives of both employers and workers agreed...
content: A revised wage structure for Bangladesh’s garment workers will come into effect in December, according to members of the newly formed wage board. Representatives of both employers and workers agreed to the timeline during the board’s meeting on 4 November. The announcement comes amid ongoing protests in Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur, where garment workers are demanding an increase in the minimum monthly wage from Tk 12,500 to Tk 30,000. Workers have also called for an end to alleged blacklisting practices and what they describe as unjust layoffs. The government formed a six-member wage board on 1 November to review the existing wage structure following widespread demonstrations and clashes between workers and law enforcement agencies. The board has begun discussions aimed at determining a revised minimum wage acceptable to both workers and employers. Meanwhile, protests continued on Monday as police dispersed demonstrators in Savar’s Hemayetpur area after they attempted to move towards the Dhaka-Aricha Highway. Law enforcement used tear gas to clear the protesters, who have been holding demonstrations for several consecutive days. The labour unrest has disrupted factory operations across several industrial zones, forcing hundreds of garment factories to temporarily suspend production and leading to road blockades in major manufacturing areas. Industry stakeholders hope the wage board’s decision and the planned implementation of a new wage structure in December will help ease tensions and restore stability to Bangladesh’s vital garment sector.

World cotton production is estimated at 25.75 million tonnes, down approximately 4% from 26.85 […] The post Consumption to Exceed Production Based on Resilient Demand in Asia appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Global cotton consumption is projected to exceed production in the 2026/27 season as output declines across several major producing countries while demand remains relatively stable, according to the November edition of Cotton This Month , published by the International Cotton Advisory Committee (ICAC). World cotton production is estimated at 25.75 million tonnes, down approximately 4% from 26.85 million tonnes in 2025/26. Global consumption, meanwhile, is projected to increase slightly to 26.10 million tonnes, compared with 25.89 million tonnes the previous season. The projections indicate that consumption will exceed production by approximately 353,000 tonnes, reversing the previous season’s production surplus of nearly 961,000 tonnes. The shift suggests a modest drawdown in global cotton inventories. Production Declines Across Major Suppliers The decline in global production reflects reduced crop prospects in several major cotton-producing countries. China’s production is projected to fall by approximately 4%, from 7.5 million tonnes to 7.2 million tonnes, while Brazil’s output is expected to decline by about 2%, from 4.25 million tonnes to 4.10 million tonnes. Production in Pakistan is also forecast to fall by approximately 17%, while the United States is expected to record a decline of about 4%. India’s production is projected to remain stable at 5.3 million tonnes, while West African output is expected to increase modestly to approximately 954,000 tonnes. The outlook remains subject to weather-related risks, particularly in India and West Africa, where irregular rainfall, drought, excessive moisture, and pest pressure could affect yields and lead to further revisions as the season progresses. content: Three years after its launch in English, Spanish, French and Turkish, Barmag’s Digital Academy online training centre for the BCF process is now also available in Chinese. Available on the e-commerce platform myBarmag.com, it offers a wide range of e-learning modules on the operation, maintenance, and repair of the Neumag BCF S+ and S8 systems. The training programme is aimed at operators, process engineers and technicians, as well as quality managers. Compact, role-based learning units, accessible via mobile and desktop devices, allow users to quickly apply the content. At the same time, the programme consistently shares Barmag’s OEM expertise regarding the operation and maintenance of the machines. In contrast to work methods that have evolved individually, all processes are standardised and followed through in complete detail. This ensures that users learn and apply the defined best practices. Progress assessments help participants internalize the contents and reinforce what they have learned and exams and certificates document their learning achievements. Feedback features can quickly clarify comprehension questions at any time. Access to the Digital Academy is granted on a location or company-specific basis. Around 450 active users have already recognised the benefits of Barmag’s digital classroom for themselves. title: All About AI: Begüm Dogru Öztekin of Refabric
summary: Refabric's Co-founder & CEO on why trust in AI will be built from an underlying fashion data layer, practical results, and consistency over time. The post All About AI: Begüm Dogru Öztekin of Refabric appeared first on The Interline .
content: Originally released in The Interline’s AI Report 2026 , this executive interview with Refabric is one of a 17-part series that sees The Interline quiz executives from companies who have either introduced new AI solutions or added meaningful new AI capabilities into their existing platforms . For more exclusive interviews, stories and opinions from different industry perspectives, and real survey feedback from voices from every level of fashion, download The AI Report 2026 . We’re observing a big disconnect (in both our own fashion-only data and in wider benchmarks from other sources) between the increasing capability and reliability of AI, in both a general sense and in discrete applications, and the lack of trust that end users place in its outputs. What does trust in your specific applications of AI look like, and how do you achieve and measure it? For us, trust is built on consistency. Every image is preprocessed, every prompt is enriched, and every request is routed through a pipeline built specifically for fashion use cases. Every ingested image is analyzed down to its finest fashion-specific attributes, construction details, fabric behavior, trim, and stitch. This is not a generic vision model with a fashion layer on top; the pipeline is built for fashion from the ground up. But we measure trust the way our customers do: in practical results. Fewer sampling rounds, fewer corrections, production-ready outcomes. We track exactly those metrics with our enterprise clients. When the output becomes reliable enough to act on without rework, trust follows naturally. Most AI tools that touch design and / or development start with one or more off-the-shelf, industry-agnostic models, and they primarily begin with quick-win visualisation and sharing as their targets. content: The UCC 672-ME combines electronic three-way needle selection on cylinder and dial with exceptional design flexibility, production efficiency and application-driven textile innovation. Terrot Textilmaschinen GmbH, the German circular knitting machinery manufacturer and a premium engineering provider within the Santoni China Group, will showcase its UCC 672-ME at ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026 in Shanghai, China. Designed for premium mattress ticking, upholstery and other demanding textile applications, the double electronic circular knitting machine combines independently programmable three-way needle selection on both cylinder and dial with high production output and extensive patterning capabilities. The technology enables manufacturers to develop sophisticated, double-sided fabric structures while increasing design flexibility and supporting efficient, application-specific textile manufacturing. Dual-sided technology expands design possibilities At the heart of the UCC 672-ME is electronic three-way needle selection on both cylinder and dial. By independently programming knit, tuck and miss actions at every feeder on both needle systems, manufacturers can create intricate jacquard patterns, three-dimensional textures, ventilation zones and reversible fabric structures with extensive design freedom. At ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026, Terrot will highlight a 38-inch UCC 672-ME configured in E20 gauge with 88 feeders and electronic three-way selection on both needle systems. The exhibition machine features a specialized mattress-fabric concept combining differentiated fabric zones, comfort-oriented construction and ventilation structures on both fabric sides. summary: Embroidery machine manufacturer ZSK has introduced an open API and direct integration with Anthropic’s Claude AI platform to its MY.ZSK 4.0 monitoring system, allowing manufacturers to analyse production data and build their own performance dashboards without programming expertise. The development is intended to make the extensive operating data generated by industrial embroidery machines more accessible […] The post ZSK brings AI-powered production analysis to embroidery appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Embroidery machine manufacturer ZSK has introduced an open API and direct integration with Anthropic’s Claude AI platform to its MY.ZSK 4.0 monitoring system, allowing manufacturers to analyse production data and build their own performance dashboards without programming expertise. The development is intended to make the extensive operating data generated by industrial embroidery machines more accessible to production managers, enabling them to identify inefficiencies, investigate recurring problems and compare performance across machines, shifts and manufacturing sites. Every connected ZSK machine generates information on stitch counts, operating speeds, thread breaks, downtime, setup times and individual embroidery designs. While this information has previously been accessible through the company’s MY.ZSK monitoring portal, the new API allows it to be integrated into manufacturers’ own enterprise resource planning (ERP), manufacturing execution systems (MES) and other production management tools. Natural language The integration with Claude takes this a stage further by allowing users to interrogate the data through natural language commands rather than having to develop their own software. Production managers can, for example, ask which embroidery designs are responsible for the most thread breaks, how much production time is lost during colour changes or whether a particular order is likely to meet its delivery deadline. Claude can retrieve and analyse the relevant machine data and present the results as charts or complete web-based dashboards, incorporating key performance indicators, machine comparisons and production trends over periods of seven, 30 or 60 days. content: From November 20 to 24, 2026, the Trützschler Group will present its latest fiber processing technologies at ITMA Asia in Shanghai, China. content: WINTERTHUR, Switzerland — November 4, 2026 — The Board of Directors of Rieter Holding Ltd. was confronted by the designated CEO, Daniel Lippuner, with additional demands regarding his compensation package, particularly his bonus. Due to irreconcilable differences, Daniel Lippuner will not assume the position. Georg Stausberg Georg Stausberg, CEO of Barmag, will assume the position of CEO of the Rieter Group with effect from November 4, 2026. Georg Stausberg has more than three decades of experience in the international textile machinery industry and has shaped the development of Barmag in various leadership positions. Under his leadership as CEO, Barmag consolidated its position as the world’s leading supplier in the man-made fiber sector. After Barmag was acquired by Rieter in February 2026, Georg Stausberg became a member of the Rieter Group’s Executive Committee. With his extensive industry expertise and his international network, Georg Stausberg is one of the most prominent leaders in the global textile machinery industry. Posted: November 4, 2026 Source: Rieter Holding Ltd.

content: The growing importance of bio-based materials in performance apparel was a central theme at the latest Functional Fabric Fair in Portland, Oregon, which attracted record attendance and more than 350 exhibitors. Held at the Oregon Convention Center from October 26-28th, the event recorded a 7% increase in attendance compared with its autumn 2025 edition, with a sold-out exhibition hall that included more than 50 companies participating for the first time. The exhibition, organised by Functional Fabric Fair powered by Performance Days, brought together textile suppliers, apparel manufacturers, designers and sourcing specialists to explore material developments for the autumn/winter 2027/28 season. A particular emphasis was placed on bio-based materials as the performance apparel industry seeks alternatives to fossil-derived fibres and finishes, while addressing increasingly demanding requirements for durability, functionality and environmental performance. The programme examined not only the potential of renewable raw materials, but also the practical challenges involved in bringing new technologies to commercial scale, including feedstock availability, traceability and certification. Cellulose Forum A new Cellulose Forum was introduced to highlight developments in natural and regenerated cellulosic fibres, ranging from hemp, flax and nettle to lyocell, modal and viscose. It joined established forums dedicated to cotton and wool, reflecting growing interest in the performance potential of natural and renewable materials. Other specialist areas explored advances in garment construction, finishing technologies and functional fabrics for sportswear, outdoor clothing, bodywear and workwear. Replacing […] The post Energy-efficient fans could cut Bangladesh’s peak power demand by up to 2,590MW: IEEFA appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: A national programme backed by bulk procurement and carbon revenue could make the switch to energy-efficient BLDC fans affordable for low-income households Key takeaways Household fans for space cooling alone account for up to 5,212 megawatts (MW) of Bangladesh’s summer power demand. Yet energy-efficient brushless direct current (BLDC) fans make up less than 2% of household fans. Replacing energy-inefficient household fans with BLDC fans could cut summer power demand by up to 2,590MW and avoid over USD4 billion in future investment in coal-fired plants. It could also save 6,913 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of electricity a year, worth BDT89.87 billion (USD0.73 billion). Households lack information on the availability of BLDC fans and their energy-saving potential. In addition to raising awareness, the Sustainable and Renewable Energy Development Authority (SREDA) should finalise standards and labels for fans to nudge consumers towards efficient models. The government could design a national programme to cut the upfront cost of BLDC fans through bulk procurement and recycle the programme’s carbon revenue to make them affordable for low-income households. Household fans add up to 5,212 megawatts (MW) to Bangladesh’s summer power demand, with usage peaking around 9PM. On 27 August 2026, the country’s peak demand hit 19,027MW at 9PM. Replacing energy-inefficient fans with the energy-efficient brushless direct current (BLDC) models could cut peak demand by up to 2,590MW, according to a new report by the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA). title: Missoni streamlines collections with Lectra PLM
summary: Italian fashion house Missoni has strengthened its product development and collection management processes with Lectra’s Kubix Link product lifecycle management (PLM) platform, achieving a 60% reduction in time spent managing and maintaining product data. The cloud-based solution has enabled Missoni to centralise product information, improve collaboration between departments and suppliers, and support the integration of […] The post Missoni streamlines collections with Lectra PLM appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Italian fashion house Missoni has strengthened its product development and collection management processes with Lectra’s Kubix Link product lifecycle management (PLM) platform, achieving a 60% reduction in time spent managing and maintaining product data. The cloud-based solution has enabled Missoni to centralise product information, improve collaboration between departments and suppliers, and support the integration of its Missoni Home business into the company’s internal operations. Founded in 1953 by Ottavio and Rosita Missoni, the Italian luxury brand is internationally recognised for its distinctive knitwear, colourful geometric patterns and innovative textile designs. Its portfolio has expanded beyond fashion into sportswear, beachwear, accessories and home furnishings. The decision to bring Missoni Home operations in-house created new requirements for managing product development, production and supply chain information. The company needed a flexible digital platform capable of supporting multiple departments while integrating with existing business systems. Missoni selected Kubix Link, building on a relationship with Lectra that began more than 25 years ago with the introduction of computer-aided design (CAD) technology. The PLM platform provides a centralised environment for managing product specifications, technical documentation and collection data, allowing internal teams and external partners to access consistent information throughout the development process. Following an initial analysis phase, the implementation progressed to a live system after 12 months, beginning with the creation of master data for a new collection. title: Rising raw material costs and price competition pressure Taiwan textile manufacturers
summary: Taiwan's textile industry is expected to face continued weakness in its core operations through the end of 2026 as rising raw material costs and intense price competition put pressure on manufacturers...
content: Taiwan's textile industry is expected to face continued weakness in its core operations through the end of 2026 as rising raw material costs and intense price competition put pressure on manufacturers' profitability. Figure: Inflation and geopolitical tensions have changed international brands' ordering patterns.Courtesy: Collected Chemical fiber producers reported that domestic raw material prices have increased by more than 30% year-on-year. Further price increases in September made it difficult for manufacturers to adjust their selling prices quickly enough to recover higher production costs. Although some manufacturers increased product prices in the second half of the year, strong market competition limited their ability to pass on additional costs. Standard-grade products faced particular pressure because of intense price competition and limited profit margins. Manufacturers are also facing competition from producers in China and Southeast Asia, where lower-priced products are affecting the performance of Taiwan's textile companies. Meanwhile, inflation and geopolitical tensions have changed international brands' ordering patterns. Brands are increasingly moving away from long-term orders toward shorter-notice orders with tighter delivery schedules. This has made production planning more difficult for manufacturers. Hong Yi Fiber Industry Co., a long-established draw-textured yarn manufacturer, continues to generate around 30% of its product mix from standard-grade yarns. The company has been shifting toward higher-value products, including composite and specialty yarns. However, its textile operations remained unprofitable in the first half of 2026. title: Change at the top for Rieter
summary: Georg Stausberg has been appointed CEO of the Rieter Group with immediate effect after a dispute over remuneration resulted in the withdrawal of the company’s previously designated chief executive, Daniel Lippuner. In an unusually frank announcement on November 4th, the Swiss textile machinery group said its board of directors had been confronted with additional demands […] The post Change at the top for Rieter appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Georg Stausberg has been appointed CEO of the Rieter Group with immediate effect after a dispute over remuneration resulted in the withdrawal of the company’s previously designated chief executive, Daniel Lippuner. In an unusually frank announcement on November 4th, the Swiss textile machinery group said its board of directors had been confronted with additional demands from Lippuner concerning his compensation package, particularly his bonus arrangements. The company said the resulting differences had proved irreconcilable and that Lippuner would therefore not be taking up the position. Instead, Rieter has appointed Georg Stausberg, CEO of Barmag, to lead the group with effect from November 4th, 2026. Stausberg brings more than three decades of experience in the international textile machinery industry, having held a succession of senior management positions at Barmag, one of the world’s leading suppliers of machinery and systems for man-made fibre production. As CEO, he played a central role in strengthening Barmag’s position in the global synthetic fibre machinery market. Following Rieter’s acquisition of Barmag in February 2026, Stausberg joined the group’s executive committee, providing him with direct involvement in the enlarged organisation. His appointment now places an established industry figure at the head of Rieter as it continues to integrate Barmag into its operations and strengthen its position across the global textile machinery market. Rieter said Stausberg’s extensive industry expertise and international network made him one of the most prominent leaders in the sector. www.rieter.com The post Change at the top for Rieter appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .

title: John Jacobs x S&N by Shantnu Nikhil: Indian Couture Meets Italian Design
title_ko: Shantnu Nikhil의 John Jacobs x S&N: 인도 패션과 이탈리아 디자인의 만남
summary: Shantnu and Nikhil make their first-ever foray into eyewear with a collaboration with John Jacobs for a bold, fashion-forward collection, now available at Lenskart stores. Two distinct design worlds. One statement-making collaboration. John Jacobs joins forces with celebrated couturiers Shantnu and Nikhil’s pret label, S&N by Shantnu Nikhil, to launch a 32-piece eyewear collection that […] The post John Jacobs x S&N by Shantnu Nikhil: Indian Couture Meets Italian Design appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Shantnu and Nikhil make their first-ever foray into eyewear with a collaboration with John Jacobs for a bold, fashion-forward collection, now available at Lenskart stores. Two distinct design worlds. One statement-making collaboration. John Jacobs joins forces with celebrated couturiers Shantnu and Nikhil’s pret label, S&N by Shantnu Nikhil, to launch a 32-piece eyewear collection that marks the designers’ first-ever venture into eyewear. Bringing together John Jacobs’ Italian design sensibilities and S&N’s distinctive design language, the collection reimagines iconic eyewear through bold design, elevated detailing and a strong point of view. Inspired by The Shape of India , the collection draws from the spirit of influential Indian leaders whose eyewear became symbols of conviction, intellect and authority. Reinterpreted for a new generation, these timeless forms get a contemporary, fashion-forward edge. The details make the statement. From the iconic S&N mark on the curve of the frame to precision metal streak detailing across the temples, every element is designed to stand out. The finishing touch? S&N’s iconic navy blue and cherry-red tape accents, tucked into the folding hinges. Together, these signature details give the range a distinctive identity, bringing the unmistakable S&N aesthetic to eyewear. Spanning eyeglasses and sunglasses across wayfarers, aviators, round frames and bold square silhouettes, the collection explores rich colours, premium refined materials and statement-making shapes. Designed to move effortlessly from everyday dressing to occasion wear, these frames bring a new edge to festive outfits, wedding looks and everything in between. Launching right in the middle of the festive season, the collection makes eyewear more than the finishing touch.

content: By K. Gopalakrishnan A legendary German circular knitting brand returns with renewed strength, a sharper customer focus and India at the heart of its global growth strategy Few names in circular knitting command the recognition, respect and technological credibility of Mayer & Cie. Founded in 1905, the German company has spent more than 120 years building a reputation around precision engineering, premium-quality circular knitting machines and technologies that have shaped generations of textile manufacturing. Over its history, the company has delivered more than 80,000 machines worldwide, establishing a formidable installed base and a brand synonymous with premium circular knitting. But even the strongest industrial brands can face extraordinary challenges. Mayer & Cie. entered insolvency proceedings in late 2025, bringing uncertainty to one of the world’s most respected names in circular knitting. What followed, however, has become an extraordinary revival story. In April 2026, the acquisition of the circular knitting machinery business by Xu Hongjie, from the family behind China’s Huixing Machinery, was formally completed, clearing the way for Mayer & Cie. Global to restart operations in Albstadt. For Xu Hongjie, the acquisition was not simply an opportunity to acquire an established machinery business. It was an opportunity to preserve a globally respected technology brand and build upon its strengths. “We are convinced of the unique value of the brand, the quality of the machines, and are deeply impressed by the technical expertise of the new team,” says Xu Hongjie. The significance of the revival lies precisely in what the new ownership has chosen not to change. Mayer & Cie. Global remains rooted in Albstadt. Design systems, product lifecycle management (PLM), enterprise resource planning (ERP), production planning, manufacturing execution systems (MES) and individual […] The post Linking the modern mill’s islands of data appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: While the textile industry has spent much of the past decade digitalising individual parts of its manufacturing chain, connecting them all together represents the next big challenge, according to the latest ITMA 2027 textile machinery exhibition blog. Design systems, product lifecycle management (PLM), enterprise resource planning (ERP), production planning, manufacturing execution systems (MES) and individual machines can all generate increasingly sophisticated data. Too often, however, it all remains trapped within separate systems. Few companies illustrate the potential of doing things differently as dramatically as Shein. The fashion giant’s rapid-response business model has been built around a highly digitalised supply chain connecting information on consumer demand with suppliers and manufacturing. “We reimagined the supply chain, which is a daunting task, and we’ve done it by digitising the small and medium-sized factories to give them visibility to see their own capacity, continued order flow and seamless efficiency,” Shein executive chairman Donald Tang has explained. Shein uses data analytics to test products in small initial batches and respond rapidly to actual demand, scaling production up or down accordingly. Whatever the wider debate surrounding the ultra-fast-fashion model, its approach demonstrates the competitive possibilities when information can move quickly between previously separate parts of the supply chain. Separate evolutions This principle is becoming increasingly relevant to textile manufacturers and not simply to meet demands for greater efficiency. title: Bangladesh and South Korea target broader economic cooperation after CEPA talks
summary: Bangladesh and South Korea have agreed to form a joint working group to increase investment, expand trade, and address business challenges. The decision follows the conclusion of negotiations on a Com...
content: Bangladesh and South Korea have agreed to form a joint working group to increase investment, expand trade, and address business challenges. The decision follows the conclusion of negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). Figure: Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, Finance and Planning Minister, shakes hands with Jung-sung Park, South Korean Trade Minister, ahead of a bilateral meeting in Seoul today. Photo: Ministry of Finance The working group will include government agencies and business chambers from both countries. It will identify investment opportunities and support joint projects through public-private partnerships (PPPs). The decision came at a meeting between Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, Finance and Planning Minister, and Jung-sung Park, South Korean Trade Minister, in Seoul on November 3, 2026. Bangladesh wants to expand its traditional textile and garment partnership with South Korea. The two countries also see opportunities in power and energy, renewable energy, electronics, semiconductors, shipbuilding and advanced manufacturing. For Bangladesh's textile and apparel industry, cooperation could bring new investment in textile technology, modern machinery and energy solutions. Renewable energy is also an important area as factories seek reliable power and lower energy costs. Bangladesh highlighted several steps to improve its investment climate. These include reducing customs duties on electronics raw materials from 26% to zero, automating capital repatriation and simplifying customs and port procedures. During the visit, the Bangladesh delegation met three major South Korean companies.Hyundai Glovis discussed opportunities in port development, logistics, automotive supply chains and smart logistics. The measures, published on October 30th, 2026, follow the introduction of provisional duties on May 12th. Effective from October 31st for a period of five years, the definitive duties range […] The post EU gets tough on nonwovens dumping appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: The European Commission has imposed definitive anti-dumping duties on imports of PET spunbond nonwovens originating in China, a decision welcomed by European industry association EDANA. The measures, published on October 30th, 2026, follow the introduction of provisional duties on May 12th. Effective from October 31st for a period of five years, the definitive duties range from 39.8% to 48.1%. The Commission’s investigation concluded that Chinese imports had increased significantly during the period examined and were being sold at unfairly low prices, causing substantial harm to the EU PET spunbond industry. It also determined that the introduction of anti-dumping measures was in the wider interests of the European Union. The duties are intended to restore fair competition and safeguard European production capacity. “We welcome the Commission’s decision to impose definitive anti-dumping measures,” said Jacques Prigneaux, market analysis and economic affairs director at EDANA. “The adoption of definitive anti-dumping duties sends an important signal that the Commission is determined to effectively address unfair trade practices on the EU market. “Restoring fair competition is essential not only for safeguarding EU production, but also for supporting the investments in innovation, sustainability and employment that are required to meet the EU’s strategic industrial ambitions.” EDANA said it would continue working with EU and national customs authorities to monitor the implementation of the measures and ensure their effective application. The association also welcomed the Commission’s investigation and its commitment to maintaining fair market conditions within the European Union. www.edana.org The post EU gets tough on nonwovens dumping appeared first on Innovation in Tex

title: Bangladesh eyes global manufacturing hub status through regional production networks
summary: Bangladesh aims to become a global manufacturing hub and export gateway by developing integrated production networks across South Asia, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and North Africa. Courtesy: Ban...
content: Bangladesh aims to become a global manufacturing hub and export gateway by developing integrated production networks across South Asia, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and North Africa. Courtesy: Bangladesh High Comission Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, Adviser to the Prime Minister on finance and planning, outlined the ambition at the inaugural session of the 29th Sustainable Development Conference in Islamabad, Pakistan, on November 2. He proposed a regional manufacturing network and said cooperation between Bangladesh and Pakistan could establish a new model of economic partnership. He also emphasized attracting investment that strengthens domestic industrial capacity, transfers technology, and creates jobs. The ambition comes as Bangladesh seeks to diversify its export base. According to Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) data, the country earned $48 billion from merchandise exports in FY2025-26. Readymade garment exports contributed $38.70 billion, accounting for approximately 80.6% of total exports. This dependence highlights the need to expand other manufacturing sectors, including leather goods, footwear, light engineering and pharmaceuticals. A World Bank-supported export diversification project has already demonstrated the employment potential of non-RMG industries, helping nearly 180,000 people secure jobs in targeted export-oriented firms. During the Pakistan visit, Haroon Akhtar Khan, Pakistan's adviser on industries and production, identified solar technology, battery manufacturing and electric vehicles as potential areas for bilateral cooperation. Discussions also covered technology transfer, joint ventures and industrial investment. title: Fakir Technologies signs deal for 6.13MWp solar project at FKL Spinning Mills
title_ko: Fakir Technologies는 FKL Spinning Mills에서 6.13MWp 태양광 프로젝트 계약을 체결했습니다.
summary: Fakir Technologies Ltd. has signed an agreement with FKL Spinning Mills Ltd. for the implementation of a 6.13 MWp On-grid Solar Power Project, in collaboration with Solar EPC Development Ltd. The agre...
content: Fakir Technologies Ltd. has signed an agreement with FKL Spinning Mills Ltd. for the implementation of a 6.13 MWp On-grid Solar Power Project, in collaboration with Solar EPC Development Ltd. The agreement marks a significant milestone in the journey towards delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions and supporting sustainable industrial development in Bangladesh. With an estimated first-year electricity generation of 8,238 MWh, the project is expected to avoid approximately 5,520 tonnes of CO₂ emissions annually. For FKL Spinning Mills Ltd., this initiative represents a major step towards reducing its environmental footprint, strengthening energy sustainability and embracing cleaner energy alternatives. For Fakir Technologies Ltd., the project further demonstrates its growing capabilities in delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions for the industrial sector. Since 2022, the company has been actively operating in Bangladesh's solar energy and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) sectors, building its expertise through global technology partnerships, project execution and integrated energy solutions. The project is being undertaken by Fakir Technologies Ltd., with Solar EPC Development Ltd. serving as its EPC partner. This 6.13 MWp project further reinforces Fakir Technologies' commitment to supporting industries in their transition towards cleaner, more efficient and sustainable energy systems. The agreement signing ceremony was held at Fakir Knitwears Ltd., Narayanganj, in the presence of senior leadership from both organizations. title: Americhem acquires Noble Biomaterials
title_ko: Americhem, Noble Biomaterials 인수
summary: US-based polymer specialist Americhem has acquired Noble Biomaterials, the developer of antimicrobial and conductive technologies for textiles and other soft surface applications. The acquisition brings Noble’s specialist technologies into Americhem’s global operations, strengthening the ability to support customers from initial product development through to commercial-scale production. Noble supplies proprietary materials technologies for applications in apparel, […] The post Americhem acquires Noble Biomaterials appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: US-based polymer specialist Americhem has acquired Noble Biomaterials, the developer of antimicrobial and conductive technologies for textiles and other soft surface applications. The acquisition brings Noble’s specialist technologies into Americhem’s global operations, strengthening the ability to support customers from initial product development through to commercial-scale production. Noble supplies proprietary materials technologies for applications in apparel, textiles, healthcare, aerospace and defence. Its established Ionic+, X-Static and Circuitex platforms provide antimicrobial, odour control and electrical conductivity functions, supported by US manufacturing operations and an extensive intellectual property portfolio developed over more than two decades. The acquisition will strengthen Americhem’s position in functional fibres and polymer solutions, particularly in healthcare and other markets requiring advanced material performance. “This is an exciting step forward for Americhem as we continue to invest in high-growth, high-demand markets,” said Americhem CEO John Richard. “Noble Biomaterials brings exceptional capabilities in antimicrobial solutions, strong commercial relationships and a reputation for quality that aligns with our values.” The financial terms of the acquisition were not disclosed. www.americhem.com www.noblebiomaterials.com The post Americhem acquires Noble Biomaterials appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .

title_ko: Trident는 ₹4,650 crore 확장 드라이브로 앞서 나가고 있습니다.
summary: Trident Limited has approved a ₹4,650-crore expansion and modernisation programme across its yarn, sheeting, paper and renewable energy businesses. Cleared by the board on November 2, 2026, the projects are… The post Trident powers ahead with ₹4,650-crore expansion drive appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: Trident Limited has approved a ₹4,650-crore expansion and modernisation programme across its yarn, sheeting, paper and renewable energy businesses. Cleared by the board on November 2, 2026, the projects are scheduled for completion in stages between December 2027 and September 2029, with funding through internal accruals and debt. Mr. Rajinder Gupta, Chairman, Trident Group The largest investment, ₹1,660 crore, will go towards a new yarn manufacturing facility at Dhar, Madhya Pradesh, with a capacity of 1,99,680 spindles. Trident has already acquired 179.2 acres of leasehold land for the project at an approximate cost of ₹106.09 crore. The facility is expected to be completed by September 30, 2029. At its existing yarn facility in Budhni, Madhya Pradesh, the company will invest ₹1,022 crore in expansion and modernisation, targeted for completion by December 31, 2027. The programme includes the addition of 99,840 spindles, replacement of 48,000 older spindles with 70,176 new spindles for finer-count yarns, and replacement of 960 older rotors with 2,400 new rotors. Trident’s existing yarn operations across Sanghera, Punjab, and Budhni have 7,46,064 spindles, 5,424 rotors and 320 air-jets. Capacity utilisation at Budhni stands at 94%. The sheeting business will receive ₹1,018 crore for the addition of 336 looms, taking its loom capacity from 504 to 840. Scheduled for completion by January 31, 2028, the expansion comes against reported capacity utilisation of 58%. In paper, Trident plans to invest ₹296 crore to add 28 tonnes per day, increasing manufacturing capacity from 479 to 507 tonnes per day. title: Car Seat, Structures and Interior Component Supplier Brose Sitech Selects Richland County, S.C. For First US Manufacturing Facility
summary: COLUMBIA, S.C. — October 28, 2026 — Brose Sitech, a supplier of car seats, structures and interior components, today announced it selects Richland County for its first U.S. manufacturing facility. The company’s $29.5 million investment will create 330 new jobs. Brose Sitech develops and produces complete seats, structures and other seat components. With its global […]
content: COLUMBIA, S.C. — October 28, 2026 — Brose Sitech, a supplier of car seats, structures and interior components, today announced it selects Richland County for its first U.S. manufacturing facility. The company’s $29.5 million investment will create 330 new jobs. Brose Sitech develops and produces complete seats, structures and other seat components. With its global headquarters in Poland, the company has 22 locations internationally, including its regional headquarters office in Detroit. Located at the Just in Time facility in the Scout Supplier Park in Blythewood, Brose Sitech’s new 140,000-square-foot facility will supply the new Scout Motors plant with complete car seat sets. Operations are expected to be online in 2027. Individuals interested in joining the Brose Sitech team should visit the company’s careers page. “Establishing our first manufacturing location in Blythewood is an important milestone for Brose Sitech. The U.S. is a significant automotive market with strong opportunities for future growth. With our new production facility, we are bringing our expertise in complete seating systems closer to our customer Scout while laying the foundation for Brose Sitech’s long-term development in North America.” -Brose Sitech Columbia Inc. Executive Vice President Juan-Carlos Kieler “With the addition of 330 new jobs in the Palmetto State, we are proud to welcome Brose Sitech to Richland County. By joining Scout Motors’ Supplier Park, the company is building on South Carolina’s position as a leader in automotive manufacturing and helping create new opportunities for our people.” -Gov. content: TEMPE, Ariz. — November 2, 2026 — Economic activity in the manufacturing sector expanded in October for the 10th consecutive month, say the nation’s supply executives in the latest ISM ® Manufacturing PMI ® Report. The report was issued today by Susan Spence, MBA, Chair of the Institute for Supply Management ® (ISM ® ) Manufacturing Business Survey Committee. “The Manufacturing PMI ® registered 55.5 percent in October, 1 percentage point above the September figure of 54.5 percent. The overall economy expanded for the 24th month in a row. (A Manufacturing PMI ® above 47.5 percent, over a period of time, generally indicates an expansion of the overall economy.) The New Orders Index expanded for the 10th consecutive month after four straight readings in contraction, registering 55.5 percent, up 0.2 percentage point compared to September’s figure of 55.3 percent. The October reading of the Production Index (59 percent) is 2.3 percentage points higher than the 56.7 percent recorded in September and the highest since November 2021 (60.5 percent). The Prices Index remained in expansion (or ‘increasing’ territory), registering 75.2 percent, a 2.7-percentage point decrease compared to September’s reading of 77.9 percent. The Backlog of Orders Index registered 54.6 percent, down 1.8 percentage points compared to the 56.4 percent recorded in September. The Employment Index reading of 52.4 percent is down 0.3 percentage point from September’s figure of 52.7 percent,” says Spence. “The Supplier Deliveries Index indicated slowing performance for the 11th month in a row after one month in ‘faster’ territory. title: Three innovations recognised at AVK Composites Awards
title_ko: AVK Composites Awards에서 인정받은 세 가지 혁신
summary: Three developments in lightweight construction, automated manufacturing and advanced fibre reinforcement have taken first places in the three categories of the 2026 AVK Innovation Awards, presented at the JEC Composites Talks DACH held in Cologne, Germany, on October 20th. Organised by AVK, the German Federation of Reinforced Plastics, the annual awards recognise advances in composite […] The post Three innovations recognised at AVK Composites Awards appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Three developments in lightweight construction, automated manufacturing and advanced fibre reinforcement have taken first places in the three categories of the 2026 AVK Innovation Awards, presented at the JEC Composites Talks DACH held in Cologne, Germany, on October 20th. Organised by AVK, the German Federation of Reinforced Plastics, the annual awards recognise advances in composite products, manufacturing processes and scientific research. Products and applications Dresden-based Anybrid secured first place in the products and applications category for a heavy-duty diamond core drill incorporating a carbon fibre-reinforced thermoplastic body in place of conventional steel. Developed with partners including Avanco Composites, Mitsui Chemicals Europe, AFPT, Hilti Kunststofftechnik and TU Dresden, the component has combined laser-based tape winding with injection moulding to produce a lightweight structure with integrated metal connections. The resulting drill assembly achieves a weight reduction of approximately 70% compared with steel, at least doubles service life and reduces its carbon footprint by around 37%. The development has successfully completed mechanical testing and practical field trials. Processes and manufacturing CompriseTec won the processes and methods category for a robotic manufacturing technology that eliminates the need for conventional moulds when producing thermoplastic composite components. Developed with the Hamburg University of Technology’s Institute of Aircraft Production Technology and Invent, the process employs two cooperating robots to shape heated, continuous fibre-reinforced thermoplastic sheets into complex geometries. summary: The European Commission's Joint Research Centre (JRC) has proposed harmonized end-of-waste (EoW) criteria for textile, textile-related and footwear waste to support reuse and remanufacturing across th...
content: The European Commission's Joint Research Centre (JRC) has proposed harmonized end-of-waste (EoW) criteria for textile, textile-related and footwear waste to support reuse and remanufacturing across the European Union. The technical report, published on 26 October 2026, aims to reduce regulatory differences among member states and establish common conditions for recovered textiles to re-enter the market as products rather than waste. Figure: Under the revised Waste Framework Directive, Member States must establish separate collection systems for used textiles from 2025. Courtesy: Collected The proposal addresses a regulatory gap in Europe's circular textile value chain. Currently, differences in national waste classifications create uncertainty for waste-management operators, textile sorters, reuse platforms, remanufacturers and downstream buyers. A harmonized framework could make it easier for businesses to handle recovered materials and trade reusable textile products across national borders. The European Environment Agency (EEA) estimated that the EU generated 6.95 million tons of textile waste in 2020, equivalent to around 16 kg per person. Of this amount, 82% came from post-consumer textiles, including used clothing and household textiles. Around 11.6 kg per person ended up in mixed household waste, while only 4.4 kg was collected separately for reuse and recycling. The challenge extends beyond waste collection. According to the EU's revised Waste Framework Directive, less than 1% of clothing waste is currently used to produce new clothing through textile-to-textile recycling. He also serves as Vice President of the Tiruppur Exporters’ Association, reflecting his contribution to the wider advancement of Tiruppur’s export industry. Under his leadership, SNQS has developed extensive manufacturing capabilities, including more than two decades of experience in conventional screen and hybrid printing. content: CLEARWATER, Fla.— November 3, 2026 — PCP Ventures LLC, a Florida-based investor group, announced that it completed the acquisition of Pellon on October 1. Pellon is a globally recognized textile brand that makes specialty materials used in everything from clothing and quilts to home décor and crafts. Pellon’s products help give finished items shape, support, softness and cushioning, and include interfacings, stabilizers, batting, fiberfill, foams and other specialty fabrics. The company, which employs approximately 95 people, produces its products at a 220,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Clearwater, Florida. Pellon has been a globally trusted name among sewists and quilters for decades, so much so that “Pellon” is widely used as the generic term for interfacing. The brand’s products are often described as the “Magic in the Middle” characterized as the hidden yet essential materials inside a project that provide the support, structure, and functionality needed to bring the finished product together. Under PCP Ventures, Pellon will continue providing products for do-it-yourself sewing enthusiasts through stores such as Walmart, Hobby Lobby and Michael’s. The company sees tremendous potential in expanding its reach to users in other industries. The market is vast, given that Pellon’s products can be used in apparel, quality, sewing, furniture and a wide range of consumer applications. Leadership Committed to the Brand PCP Ventures is led by a Florida-based investment group representing family offices with combined assets of close to $1 billion, including Adam Schoenbaum and Ron Ciganek. content: CARY, N.C. — November 3, 2026 — FiltXPO 2026 brought together filtration industry leaders, manufacturers, researchers, product developers and technology innovators Oct. 28-29 at the Minneapolis Convention Center in Minneapolis, Minnesota. Organized by INDA, the Association of the Nonwoven Fabrics Industry, FiltXPO provided a forum for industry professionals to discover innovative filtration technologies, explore emerging market opportunities, exchange technical expertise and build business relationships. The two-day event featured an exhibition showcasing filtration products, materials, components and manufacturing technologies, and the Advances in Filtration Technical Conference, which addressed the trends and challenges shaping the future of air, gas, water and liquid filtration. FiltXPO 2026 Innovation Award Winners Announced A highlight of the event was the presentation of the FiltXPO 2026 Innovation Awards, recognizing advancements in filtration technology, performance and sustainability. The winners were honored in two categories: Air/Gas Filtration Innovation Award Solberg Manufacturing Inc. — Fully Automated Liquid Management System Imagine giving a vacuum system the ability to continuously manage heavy liquid loads with less operator involvement. Liquids are continuously captured and removed while low pressure loss supports vacuum performance, helping protect valuable equipment, simplify liquid management, and reduce maintenance demands. content: GREENSBORO, N.C.— November 3, 2026 — Kontoor Brands, Inc. today announced it has completed the sale of the Lee® business to Authentic Brands Group. “I want to thank the Kontoor team for the tremendous effort that drove the successful completion of this transaction,” said Scott Baxter, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of the Board of Kontoor Brands. “We now have a more focused, growth-oriented portfolio positioned to deliver stronger returns for our shareholders.” “We are grateful to the Lee team for their contributions to Kontoor and wish them well as they write the next chapter of the brand’s iconic history,” Baxter added. title: BAPEX discovers 97.69 BCF gas well in Noakhali
summary: Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company Limited (BAPEX) has discovered an estimated 97.69 BCF of natural gas at the Sundalpur South-1 exploratory well in Noakhali’s Companiganj. The di...
content: Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company Limited (BAPEX) has discovered an estimated 97.69 BCF of natural gas at the Sundalpur South-1 exploratory well in Noakhali’s Companiganj. The discovery is expected to strengthen local energy security and support efforts to reduce dependence on imported fuels. Courtesy: Collected The discovery was confirmed on 2 November through a gas flare test after drilling operations at the well in Rampur Union were completed. According to BAPEX, the estimated gas reserves are spread across two zones of the well. The gas is valued at approximately Tk 5,809 crore at consumer-level prices, while the well is expected to supply 15 million cubic feet of gas per day to the national grid. Gas extraction from the well is expected to continue for the next 20 years. Drilling at the Sundalpur South-1 exploratory well began on 8 July this year using BAPEX's Bijoy-10 rig. The operation reached a depth of 3,289 meters and was financed jointly by the government and BAPEX. The Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources undertook the drilling initiative based on the findings of BAPEX's three-dimensional (3D) seismic survey. Mohammad Mozammel Haque, Project Director of the Sundalpur South-1 exploratory well, confirmed the discovery. He said further observation and a Drill Stem Test (DST) over the next 15 days would determine whether oil or any other substance is also present in the well. The discovery comes as Bangladesh continues to explore domestic gas resources to strengthen energy security and reduce dependence on imported fuels.

title: Bangladesh needs $2bn investment to achieve 4,000mw rooftop solar target
summary: Bangladesh needs around $2 billion (Tk 25,000 crore) in investment, along with skilled manpower and stronger infrastructure, to achieve its 4,000MW rooftop solar target within a year. Figure: Banglad...
content: Bangladesh needs around $2 billion (Tk 25,000 crore) in investment, along with skilled manpower and stronger infrastructure, to achieve its 4,000MW rooftop solar target within a year. Figure: Bangladesh needs $2bn investment to achieve 4,000mw rooftop solar target. Courtesy: Collected The observations were shared during a discussion titled “Rooftop Solar: Is Adding 4,000MW in a Year Viable?” held at The Daily Star Centre in Dhaka. Energy experts say the ambitious goal is achievable, but success will depend on financing, policy support, grid upgrades, and rapid capacity building. Despite acknowledging the challenges, experts agreed that the target is achievable if bureaucratic obstacles are removed and financing mechanisms are strengthened. However, they emphasized that success will depend not only on installing solar panels but also on developing a skilled workforce, upgrading the electricity grid and ensuring long-term maintenance. Dipal C Barua, Founder and Chairman of Bright Green Energy Foundation, stressed the need to prioritize decentralized renewable energy alongside conventional power generation. He argued that Bangladesh's reliance on imported fuel could be reduced by encouraging households, businesses and farmers to generate electricity through rooftop solar, small wind turbines and biogas systems. Barua said both conventional power and solar energy could have developed simultaneously over the years, helping the country avoid recurring power shortages and load-shedding. He also highlighted opportunities in solar irrigation and agrivoltaics and called for stronger quality control measures to ensure consumer confidence in renewable technologies. title_ko: 6.13 MWp 태양광 프로젝트: Fakir Technologies, FKL Spinning Mills Ltd.와 계약 체결
summary: Dhaka, 3 November 2026: Fakir Technologies Ltd. has signed an agreement with FKL Spinning Mills Ltd. for the implementation of a 6.13 MWp On-grid Solar Power Project, in collaboration with Solar EPC Development Ltd. The agreement marks a significant milestone in the journey towards delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions and supporting sustainable industrial development in […] The post 6.13 MWp Solar Project: Fakir Technologies Signs Agreement with FKL Spinning Mills Ltd. appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Dhaka, 3 November 2026: Fakir Technologies Ltd. has signed an agreement with FKL Spinning Mills Ltd. for the implementation of a 6.13 MWp On-grid Solar Power Project , in collaboration with Solar EPC Development Ltd. The agreement marks a significant milestone in the journey towards delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions and supporting sustainable industrial development in Bangladesh. With an estimated first-year electricity generation of 8,238 MWh , the project is expected to avoid approximately 5,520 tonnes of CO ₂ emissions annually . For FKL Spinning Mills Ltd., this initiative represents a major step towards reducing its environmental footprint, strengthening energy sustainability and embracing cleaner energy alternatives. For Fakir Technologies Ltd., the project further demonstrates its growing capabilities in delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions for the industrial sector. Since 2022, the company has been actively operating in Bangladesh’s solar energy and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) sectors, building its expertise through global technology partnerships, project execution and integrated energy solutions. The project is being undertaken by Fakir Technologies Ltd., with Solar EPC Development Ltd. serving as its EPC partner. This 6.13 MWp project further reinforces Fakir Technologies’ commitment to supporting industries in their transition towards cleaner, more efficient and sustainable energy systems. The agreement signing ceremony was held at Fakir Knitwears Ltd., Narayanganj , in the presence of senior leadership from both organizations. Held at the Oregon Convention Center from 26-28 October, the event attracted its highest attendance to date, up 7% compared with […] The post Functional Fabric Fair reaches new heights appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Functional Fabric Fair powered by Performance Days has reported record attendance at its Fall 2026 edition in Portland, reinforcing its growing importance as an international sourcing and innovation platform for the performance textiles industry. Held at the Oregon Convention Center from 26-28 October, the event attracted its highest attendance to date, up 7% compared with Fall 2025. The exhibition hall sold out with more than 350 exhibitors, while the opening OIA Catalyst Conference also reached capacity, bringing together more than 300 industry professionals. The results reflect the increasing significance of Functional Fabric Fair and its partnership with Performance Days, which together provide an expanding international platform connecting textile manufacturers, technology developers, apparel brands and sourcing professionals. With an established presence in Europe through Performance Days in Munich and a growing programme of Functional Fabric Fair events across the United States, the partnership is strengthening its position as a year-round meeting point for the global functional textiles industry. As the show continues to grow, it has become an even more effective platform for expanding our network and supporting our long-term growth The Portland exhibition attracted product developers, designers, sourcing specialists and senior executives from leading international brands, including Adidas, Arc’teryx, Columbia Sportswear, HOKA, Lululemon, New Balance, Nike, Patagonia, Under Armour and Vuori. summary: When the Factory Stops, Everyone’s Clock Keeps Running Imagine a factory on a November morning. Fabric is ready. Some garments are waiting for their final inspection. A merchandiser opens an email from a buyer: “Can you confirm the shipment date?” Outside, workers are gathering. Inside, management is deciding whether production can continue safely. content: When the Factory Stops, Everyone’s Clock Keeps Running Imagine a factory on a November morning. Fabric is ready. Some garments are waiting for their final inspection. A merchandiser opens an email from a buyer: “Can you confirm the shipment date?” Outside, workers are gathering. Inside, management is deciding whether production can continue safely. The shipment clock is still running. So is the worker’s rent. So is the factory’s interest bill Figure: Ruhul Talukder, Managing Director, Ruhrose.com That is what makes Bangladesh’s current garment crisis so difficult. People standing on different sides of the factory gate are worried about the same thing: their future. The challenge is finding a way forward that they can trust. Behind the headlines are two kinds of pressure: Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. Their protests also include concerns about blacklisting and the reinstatement of dismissed workers. Reports of road blockades, clashes and attacks on property show how serious the situation has become. For workers, the discussion starts with daily life: food, rent, transport and the cost of supporting a family. For factory owners, it starts with a different calculation: the price agreed with the buyer, the cost of materials, wages, energy and the money left after shipment. Neither calculation disappears because the other side is struggling. A worker cannot pay rent with an explanation about low margins. A factory cannot meet a higher wage bill simply by wishing buyers would pay more. This is where leadership matters. The industry needs a workable agreement that recognises both realities. summary: In an exclusive interview at TITAS 2026, Justin Huang, President of the Taiwan Textile Federation (TTF), discusses the material innovations and commercial decisions behind Taiwan’s drive to recover more value… The post Taiwan’s Textile Ambition: Making Responsibility a Competitive Advantage appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: In an exclusive interview at TITAS 2026, Justin Huang, President of the Taiwan Textile Federation (TTF), discusses the material innovations and commercial decisions behind Taiwan’s drive to recover more value from textile waste. By Nithin Kumar A performance fabric earns its reputation through what it does for the wearer. For Justin Huang, its value increasingly extends to what happens after use: whether its materials can be recovered and made useful again. Justin Huang, President of the Taiwan Textile Federation (TTF) Speaking exclusively to The Textile Magazine at the 30th Taipei Innovative Textile Application Show, TITAS 2026, Huang argues that material recovery can strengthen Taiwan’s position with global brands. With relatively high labour and energy costs, he says, Taiwanese suppliers must give international customers compelling reasons to choose them. He points to years of investment in materials and manufacturing processes intended to reduce environmental impact. In his account, taking responsibility for textile waste is becoming part of the value Taiwan offers its customers. Giving textiles another life A central priority is the move beyond PET-bottle recycling towards textile-to-textile recycling. Bringing discarded fabrics and garments back into fibre production would allow the industry to recover more of the materials contained in its own products. The difficulty begins with composition. Garments commonly combine different fibres, complicating the recovery process. Materials must be identified and sorted, while dyes and other unwanted substances may need to be removed. title: Techtextil And Texprocess 2028 Strengthen Networking And Business Opportunities Along The Textile Value Chain
title_ko: Techtextil 및 Texprocess 2028, 섬유 가치 사슬을 따라 네트워킹 및 비즈니스 기회 강화
summary: FRANKFURT AM MAIN, Germany — November 3, 2026 — Techtextil and Texprocess 2028 bring relevant market players even closer together. The focus is on the interfaces between materials, technology and processing – where innovations, new applications and business contacts emerge. The optimised hall layout supports this networking across the exhibition grounds, with short distances and […]
content: FRANKFURT AM MAIN, Germany — November 3, 2026 — Techtextil and Texprocess 2028 bring relevant market players even closer together. The focus is on the interfaces between materials, technology and processing – where innovations, new applications and business contacts emerge. The optimised hall layout supports this networking across the exhibition grounds, with short distances and an efficient route along the various stages of textile production and processing. Companies can register at early-booking rates until the end of November. The first renowned exhibitors have already registered. Techtextil-Texprocess 2026 Photo: Messe Frankfurt / Pietro Sutera Volatile markets, cost pressures and changing supply chains are challenging the global textile industry. At the same time, material innovations and new technologies such as AI are opening up additional applications and business opportunities. Collaboration along the value chain is essential. Techtextil and Texprocess bring together relevant market players in Frankfurt from 4 to 7 April 2028 who are shaping this transformation – from research and technology providers to manufacturers and processors as well as users from a wide range of industries. A major benefit lies in running the two leading trade fairs concurrently: together, they cover key production and processing stages at a single location, giving exhibitors access to new partners and fields of application beyond their own markets. Visitor behaviour also shows how closely the potential of the two events is intertwined: in 2026, 87 percent of Texprocess trade visitors also attended Techtextil. Conversely, 68 percent took advantage of what Texprocess had to offer. Around 80 percent of exhibitors achieved their trade fair objectives. First leading industry players commit

title: 효성, 제주에 멸종위기 물장군 40개체 방사
summary: 효성이 제주에서 인공증식한 멸종위기곤충 물장군 40개체를 자연에 방사했다. 지난해 비단벌레 방사에 이은 생물다양성 보전 활동으로, 임직원이 생태계 복원에 참여하는 기회를 확대하고 있다.효성은 지난 10월 29~30일 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 성산읍 일대에서 물장군 방사 행사를 진행했다. 행사에는 ㈜효성과 효성티앤씨, 효성중공업, 효성화학 등 4개 계열사 임직원이 참여했다.물장군은 연못과 습지에 서식하는 대형 수서곤충으로 습지 생태계의 상위 포식자다. 습지 감소와 농약 사용에 따른 수질오염 등으로 서식지와 개체 수가 줄어 멸종위기 야생
