title: US trade show returns to Dhaka with $5 billion investment target
summary: The United States is seeking to expand its business and investment engagement with Bangladesh as the American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh (AmCham) prepares to host the 30th US Trade Show in Dhak...
content: The United States is seeking to expand its business and investment engagement with Bangladesh as the American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh (AmCham) prepares to host the 30th US Trade Show in Dhaka from November 5 to 7. The event comes as both countries look to strengthen trade relations, attract new investment and expand cooperation in technology, energy and manufacturing. The American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh holds a special press conference ahead of the ‘30th US Trade Show 2026’ at the Hotel InterContinental in the capital on November 2. | The three-day exhibition will take place at Hotel InterContinental Dhaka after a gap of two and a half years. It will showcase American products, services and technologies while providing a platform for business networking and investment discussions. AmCham announced the event at a press conference on November 2. According to the organizers, 43 exhibitors, including 36 companies and seven startups, will participate through 63 booths. Syed Mohammad Kamal, President, AmCham, said the chamber had previously set a target of attracting $5 billion in US investment to Bangladesh over the next five years. He emphasized that energy security would be essential to achieving this goal. "If this exhibition helps bring 10 to 12 new American companies to Bangladesh, that itself will be a major achievement," he said. The investment target comes against a backdrop of expanding bilateral economic relations. According to the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR), total US-Bangladesh goods and services trade reached an estimated $13.7 billion in 2025, increasing 10.3% from 2024. title: Wage protests disrupt operations at over 300 garment factories
summary: Garment manufacturing operations faced disruptions across major industrial zones in Gazipur, Ashulia and Mirpur on Tuesday as workers continued demonstrations demanding higher wages. More than 300 fac...
content: Garment manufacturing operations faced disruptions across major industrial zones in Gazipur, Ashulia and Mirpur on Tuesday as workers continued demonstrations demanding higher wages. More than 300 factories announced temporary holidays or experienced production stoppages amid the ongoing situation. Courtesy: Collected According to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), 161 factories in Gazipur declared general holidays, while production remained suspended at 93 factories in the Savar, Ashulia and Zirani areas. Another 52 factories were also reported closed following work stoppages by workers. In Gazipur, demonstrations took place at several industrial locations, including Naojor, Bhogra, Palli Bidyut and Chandra. Workers attempted to block sections of the Dhaka-Tangail Highway, affecting traffic movement between Joydebpur Chowrasta and Naojor. Additional law enforcement personnel were deployed to manage the situation and maintain traffic flow. Similar disruptions were reported in Ashulia, where workers gathered at several points along the Baipail-Abdullahpur road. Although many workers initially joined their regular shifts, some factories subsequently suspended operations as a precautionary measure amid concerns over possible disruptions. The situation also affected industrial activity in Mirpur, where workers staged demonstrations in the Mirpur 11 area. Police and other security personnel were deployed in the affected locations to maintain order and facilitate a return to normal activities. In Gazipur, members of the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) were also deployed alongside police to support security operations. content: BRIDGWATER, England— November 3, 2026 — Ned Dorbin has been announced as Chief Executive Officer of Nonwovenn and of Technical Materials Group (TMG), as the combined businesses look to accelerate growth, working towards ambitious targets over the next few years. Ned is familiar with Nonwovenn having spent six years as a non-executive director between 2016 and 2022. He has 19 years of experience as a private equity investor, supporting the growth of businesses across a wide range of sectors with funding and strategic board input. Ned Dorbin Nonwovenn and TMG plan to significantly increase their scale over the coming years through a combination of organic growth and acquisitions. As CEO, Ned will be responsible for leading the businesses through this next phase, providing strategic direction and driving commercial performance. His experience of working with management teams, supporting investment decisions and scaling businesses will be central to delivering these ambitions. Former CEO Andrew Brownlow remains an important part of the leadership team, with an increased focus on strategic projects, capital investment programmes and operational development. Ned Dorbin, Chief Executive Officer at Nonwovenn and Technical Materials Group, said: “I’m delighted to be joining Nonwovenn and TMG. Having previously worked with Nonwovenn, I know how well positioned the business is to expand and capitalise on the opportunities ahead. content: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman joined the opening ceremony of Bangladesh Solar Expo-2026 in the city this morning as the chief guest. The inaugural ceremony began at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in the capital, said Prime Minister’s Deputy Press Secretary Jahidul Islam Rony. The Power Division and the Infrastructure Development Company Limited (IDCOL) jointly organised the expo for the first time with the theme “Utilise Every Inch of Rooftop, Increase Income through Solar Power”. Chaired by Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood Tuku, it was also joined by State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit, Finance Secretary Dr Md Khairuzzaman Mozumder and Power Division Secretary Mirana Mahrukh. Ministers, state ministers, members of parliament, secretaries and senior government officials from different ministries also attended the programme. The developments will be demonstrated at ITMA Asia 2026 in Shanghai from November 20-24, alongside a new collection of warp knitted fabrics designed to reproduce […] The post Extending warp knitting into finer fashion fabrics appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Karl Mayer has further developed its TM Weft warp knitting machine for fashion and apparel applications, introducing a finer E 36 gauge, greater patterning flexibility and improved yarn tension control. The developments will be demonstrated at ITMA Asia 2026 in Shanghai from November 20-24, alongside a new collection of warp knitted fabrics designed to reproduce the appearance of woven textiles while retaining the production and performance advantages of warp knitting. The company’s WovenLike concept combines the appearance and texture of woven fabrics with the flexibility, wrinkle resistance and ease of care associated with warp knitted constructions. It also offers opportunities for more efficient production, particularly when processing challenging materials such as linen, acetate and decorative effect yarns. The latest developments to the TM Weft include an E 36 gauge option for producing finer fabrics and a new EL pattern drive, allowing greater flexibility and speed in pattern development. Yarn tension is now continuously regulated rather than controlled through the previous system, simplifying operation and supporting more consistent fabric quality. The latest developments to the TM Weft include a new EL pattern drive. © Karl Mayer To illustrate the machine’s capabilities, Karl Mayer’s Textile Innovation Center has developed two contrasting fabric ranges for presentation at ITMA Asia. The first comprises dense, textured constructions intended for autumn and winter apparel. These include a crêpe fabric incorporating Lycra T400 for stretch and shape retention, a bouclé construction featuring metallic yarn accents and a floral design produced using a burnout technique to create areas of transparency within an otherwise closed surface. content: GREENSBORO, N.C.— October 29, 2026 — Unifi, Inc., the makers of REPREVE ® and one of the world’s leading innovators in recycled and synthetic yarns, today released operating results for the first fiscal quarter ended September 27, 2026. Highlights Net sales were $127.9 million, a decrease of 5.7% from the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Revenues from REPREVE Fiber products were $36.4 million and represented 29% of net sales, compared to $39.3 million or 29% of net sales for the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Gross profit was $12.5 million and gross margin was 9.8%, compared to gross profit of $3.4 million and gross margin of 2.5% for the first quarter of fiscal 2026. SG&A expenses were $11.5 million, a decrease of 4.1% from the first quarter of fiscal 2026, primarily driven by cost reduction efforts. Net loss was $2.0 million, or $0.11 per share, compared to a net loss of $11.4 million, or $0.62 per share, for the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Adjusted EBITDA* was $6.1 million, compared to a loss of $(2.5) million for the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Cash provided by operating activities was $3.7 million during the first quarter of fiscal 2027, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of positive cash generation. Debt principal was $90.9 million and Net Debt* was $64.8 million at September 27, 2026. Continued efforts across innovation and traceability through the introductions of CofiraTM, a versatile dual function yarn, Resist2OTM Pro, an advanced water-resistant yarn, and YarnProofTM, supporting compliance with yarn-forward requirements in North and Central America. content: Nipaş Tekstil upgraded its Rieter cards C 80 with Carding Gap Control (CGC) to improve sliver quality and increase productivity. The modernization enables the mill to operate with consistently high quality at higher production speeds while reducing maintenance efforts. Fig. 1: Carding Gap Control automatically maintains the optimal carding gap under all conditions Fig. 3: Watch the video to find out more about Nipas Tekstil’s experience with CGC Carding lays the foundation for a stable, efficient spinning process and a high-quality end product. A key parameter in achieving this is the carding gap – the distance between the flats and the cylinder – which directly affects both quality and performance. Carding Gap Control (CGC) automatically maintains the optimal gap under changing operating conditions, ensuring that the full potential of the 40 active flats is utilized. The contact-free system continuously monitors the distance between needle tips and cylinder clothing and adjusts the flat setting as required (Fig. 1). Improved quality with CGC Fig. 2: Ring-spinning manager Ömer Mutlu highlights how the Carding Gap Control is benefitting Nipaş Tekstil The benefits are clearly reflected in daily production. Ömer Mutlu, Ring Spinning Mill Manager at Nipaş Tekstil in Türkiye, states: “The modernization of the cards C 80 with CGC has significantly improved yarn quality.” He also highlights that the automatic control of the flat settings enables consistently high sliver quality while supporting higher production speeds (Fig. 2). title: What Should A Fashion AI Lead Actually Do?
summary: Selecting and implementing technology has never been the hardest part of transformation, and AI is no different. A set of hard-learned guidelines for today’s AI leaders. The post What Should A Fashion AI Lead Actually Do? appeared first on The Interline .
content: This article was originally released in The Interline’s AI Report 2026 . Including profiles and exclusive interviews with 17 AI companies, stories and opinions from 12 different industry perspectives, and real survey feedback from around 100 voices from every level of fashion, bottled and analysed, The AI Report 2026 is essential reading for anyone interested in AI for fashion. I’ve seen a lot of AI Lead job descriptions in the past 6 months, and they all ask for the same things: a deep technical background, experience in data science or IT transformation, and fluency across multiple tech stacks. They are, in other words, technology roles. That feels wrong to me. I held exactly this kind of role at G-Star RAW for close to three years, and when I look at those job descriptions now, I notice what’s missing more than what’s there. I know, first-hand, that the hardest parts of leading AI in a fashion organisation have almost nothing to do with technology. In this article, I want to explain what those missing pieces are, what I think it looks like to solve them, and how you can apply some of what I learned to your own AI strategies and transformations. Piece 1: don’t underestimate the friction built into what seems like a straightforward vision for the future. When we launched Maia, an AI-powered back-office employee at G-Star, the original problem we’d set out to solve was straightforward, well-scoped, and it had a clear value return. Our employee support teams, covering corporate and retail across multiple offices and languages, were being overwhelmed with support tickets. Hundreds of questions, often the same requests repeated for different people, in different languages, across different time zones. It was unsustainable and it was slowing down operations. content: The American Apparel & Footwear Association (AAFA) has urged the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) to address foreign trade barriers and provide greater certainty in US tariff policies. They warn that rising duties and regulatory restrictions are increasing costs for apparel, footwear, and travel goods companies. Figure:Total US tariffs collected on apparel, footwear, and travel goods reached $28.44 billion in 2025, up 68% from $16.89 billion in 2024. In its October 29 submission to the USTR's 2027 National Trade Estimate (NTE) Report on Foreign Trade Barriers, AAFA identified trade-related challenges across 12 countries, including China, India, Japan, Indonesia, Mexico, and Canada. The association said tariffs, customs procedures, technical standards, and import restrictions are disrupting supply chains and limiting market access. Rising tariffs increase industry costs According to data prepared by Trade Partnership Worldwide, LLC, the average trade-weighted tariff rate on US apparel imports increased from 14.70% in 2024 to 24.56% in 2025. Footwear tariffs rose from 12.26% to 23.75%, while travel goods tariffs increased from 13.85% to 22.83%. Total US tariffs collected on apparel, footwear, and travel goods reached $28.44 billion in 2025, up 68% from $16.89 billion in 2024. Through August 2026, the industry had paid another $17.90 billion, including $8.23 billion in additional duties imposed under presidential trade authorities. AAFA said overlapping tariffs under Sections 301, 232, 122, and 338 are making sourcing and long-term planning more difficult. It called for preventing multiple tariffs from applying to the same products, removing duties on manufacturing inputs and machinery, and providing sufficient notice before introducing new measures.

title: VistaPrint triples apparel production speed
title_ko: VistaPrint는 의류 생산 속도를 3배로 향상시킵니다.
summary: VistaPrint has increased its digital garment printing capacity by approximately 25,000 units per week following the installation of a Kornit Digital Apollo system, which is delivering production speeds around three times faster than its previous process. The investment is enabling the print and design company to reduce production turnaround times to approximately a day, while […] The post VistaPrint triples apparel production speed appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: VistaPrint has increased its digital garment printing capacity by approximately 25,000 units per week following the installation of a Kornit Digital Apollo system, which is delivering production speeds around three times faster than its previous process. The investment is enabling the print and design company to reduce production turnaround times to approximately a day, while improving operational efficiency and lowering production costs. Serving millions of small and medium-sized businesses across Europe, the United States, Canada and Australia, VistaPrint has expanded well beyond its original business card printing activities to offer a wide range of customised products, including apparel, promotional materials, packaging and signage. The company has worked with Israel-headquartered Kornit Digital since 2007, progressively upgrading its digital garment printing operations through successive generations of technology, including the Kornit Atlas and Atlas MAX systems. The latest investment in Apollo represents a further step towards high-volume, on-demand apparel manufacturing, allowing VistaPrint to respond more quickly to incoming orders while reducing the handling and labour requirements associated with garment production. The installation was supported by online training ahead of commissioning and an on-site Kornit technician during the first six months of operation. VistaPrint reached full utilisation across three production shifts approximately three months after production began. www.kornit.com www.vistaprint.com The post VistaPrint triples apparel production speed appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .

summary: Picanol will introduce a new generation of airjet weaving machines at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026 in Shanghai from November 20–24th, extending its portfolio into the market for basic woven fabrics. The new AirOne loom has been developed specifically for this segment and features a newly designed crank shedding motion, combining high productivity with low […] The post Picanol enters basic fabrics market appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Picanol will introduce a new generation of airjet weaving machines at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026 in Shanghai from November 20–24th, extending its portfolio into the market for basic woven fabrics. The new AirOne loom has been developed specifically for this segment and features a newly designed crank shedding motion, combining high productivity with low energy consumption, advanced digital capabilities and ease of operation. The launch follows extensive market research, R&D and field testing, and represents an important expansion of Picanol’s airjet weaving portfolio. AirOne will complement the established OmniPlus-i Connect, providing mills producing basic fabrics with an alternative designed around their specific production requirements. The machine incorporates a range of Picanol’s existing innovations and patented technologies, with particular emphasis on operational efficiency, sustainability and simplified machine control. “AirOne represents a special launch for Picanol,” says Johan Verstraete, vice president of weaving machines at Picanol. “This new machine platform brings together all the strengths that define Picanol today, from high performance and low energy consumption to digital capabilities and ease of operation. At the same time, it empowers us to enter a new market segment.” He adds that the company’s sales and service teams are looking forward to making Picanol technology accessible to a broader range of weaving mills. At the Shanghai exhibition, Picanol will demonstrate three machines on its stand F01 in Hall 3. The new AirOne will be producing poplin fabric, alongside an OmniPlus-i Connect weaving ladieswear fabrics and a Supermax rapier weaving machine producing denim. content: AI-powered automation, digital integration and flexible spinning technology to take center stage October 2026, Italy: Savio will showcase its latest advancements in winding and spinning technology at ITMA ASIA Shanghai 2026, highlighting the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI), automation and digital integration in textile manufacturing. The company will focus on two flagship machines: Proxima Smartconer®, its next-generation winding platform, and Lybra Smartspinner®, a versatile air-jet spinning solution. The innovations are designed to help textile manufacturers improve productivity, optimize energy consumption, enhance yarn quality and reduce processing costs while supporting more flexible and data-driven production. Proxima Smartconer®: Intelligent Winding for Higher Performance Savio’s Proxima Smartconer® is available in a comprehensive range of configurations, including fully automatic, manual feeding, cone-to-cone, Duo Lot and large bobbin feeding for the carded wool sector. The platform combines energy-saving technologies, optimized bobbin flow and AI-powered functions with Savio Insight, a web-based system for real-time production monitoring and control. Savio Insight enables remote machine setup, data tracking and performance analysis, helping manufacturers make informed decisions and improve winding process management. Another key innovation is a newly designed and patented suction nozzle in the preparation area. The component improves yarn-end capture efficiency while reducing energy consumption, contributing to lower operating costs without compromising reliability and quality. Held from 27-29 October 2026 at the Palais des Festivals in Cannes, the exhibition brought together leading European manufacturers of fabrics […] The post MarediModa Cannes signals renewed confidence appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: The 24th edition of MarediModa Cannes closed on an encouraging note, with renewed confidence among European textile manufacturers and international buyers, alongside the introduction of new creative formats and trend directions for Spring/Summer 2028. Held from 27-29 October 2026 at the Palais des Festivals in Cannes, the exhibition brought together leading European manufacturers of fabrics and accessories for beachwear, underwear and athleisure. More than 100 collections for Summer 2028 were presented, offering buyers an overview of developments in textile design, material innovation and performance. Despite continuing geopolitical and economic uncertainty, MarediModa reported results in line with the previous year, with no decline in overall activity. Organisers highlighted a more focused approach among visiting buyers, with greater attention to collection development, material selection and planning for future seasons. Claudio Taiana, President of MarediModa, said the results suggested a gradual return to confidence following a period of stagnation. “We had expected this edition to mark an acceleration after a period of stagnation linked to the international geopolitical situation. The figures are consistent with a return to programming and planning, reflected in more considered choices, closer examination of collections and a positive, vibrant atmosphere,” he said. Taiana also emphasised the exhibition’s role in promoting European textile manufacturing, particularly its combination of technical expertise, product quality and creative development. © MarediModa A significant addition to this year’s event was the inaugural Cannes Fashion Show, a new presentation format designed to demonstrate the creative and technological potential of fabrics through finished garments

content: The latest developments in hosiery technology, sustainable materials and artificial intelligence took centre stage at Legwear Innovation Day 2026, held last week at the Fulgar Event Space in Castel Goffredo, Italy. Organised by The Lycra Company in collaboration with Fulgar, the annual event brought together nearly 150 representatives from leading hosiery companies to explore market developments, emerging technologies and the fashion trends expected to shape the 2027/2028 season. The event reinforced the importance of collaboration and innovation within Italy’s historic hosiery manufacturing district, combining technical presentations with an immersive fashion performance showcasing new legwear concepts. Opening the programme, Ettore Manfrotto, Account Manager Brand & Retail at The Lycra Company, welcomed delegates before Alice Sperindio, EMEA Legwear Sales Manager, outlined the company’s activities across Italy and Europe. She highlighted opportunities to strengthen collaboration throughout the hosiery supply chain and support the development of new products and markets. summary: Garment industry leaders met Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Monday, 2 November, to discuss the ongoing labour unrest and its impact on factory operations and exports. The meeting was held at the M...
content: Garment industry leaders met Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Monday, 2 November, to discuss the ongoing labour unrest and its impact on factory operations and exports. The meeting was held at the Ministry of Home Affairs at the Secretariat in Dhaka. Prime Minister’s Adviser Mahdi Amin, Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury, garment industry representatives and senior law enforcement officials, including Dhaka Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed, attended the meeting. The discussion comes amid continued protests by garment workers demanding a higher minimum wage. The unrest has disrupted production in several industrial areas and raised concerns over factory operations, shipment schedules and export performance. Following Monday’s meeting, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed was briefing journalists on the discussions and the government’s next steps. Follow for more details....

Escalating production costs, energy supply constraints, downward pricing pressure, global trade uncertainty, and the forthcoming graduation from Least Developed Country (LDC) status are collectively challenging the sector’s long-term competitiveness. The path forward is not simply about […] The post Navigating Challenges and Securing Future Growth of Bangladesh RMG Sector appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Bangladesh RMG Industry: Navigating Challenges and Securing Future Growth Bangladesh’s Ready-Made Garment (RMG) industry stands at a pivotal moment. Escalating production costs, energy supply constraints, downward pricing pressure, global trade uncertainty, and the forthcoming graduation from Least Developed Country (LDC) status are collectively challenging the sector’s long-term competitiveness. Black,blue, grey and white t-shirts on hangers on gray background The path forward is not simply about producing larger volumes at lower prices. Sustained growth will require a strategic shift toward operational efficiency, productivity improvement, value-added products, stronger backward integration, and deeper collaboration between manufacturers and global retailers. The Role of International Buyers Building a resilient and sustainable apparel supply chain is a shared responsibility. To support long-term industry growth, international buyers should: • Provide greater visibility through reliable order forecasts and capacity commitments. • Avoid excessive price pressures that compromise sustainable manufacturing practices. • Participate in funding significant product, technology, and sustainability innovations where appropriate. • Engage suppliers earlier in product development, sourcing, and planning processes. • Recognize and reward measurable improvements in quality, productivity, compliance, and environmental performance. Stronger buyer-supplier partnerships will enhance both commercial outcomes and supply chain resilience. content: Groz-Beckert will present a broad portfolio of textile machinery components, precision tools and digital services at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026, taking place from 20-24 November in Shanghai, China. The German manufacturer will showcase innovations across knitting, weaving, nonwovens, sewing, tufting and spinning in Hall 4.1, Booth D41. Energy efficiency, process reliability and solutions for increasingly demanding textile applications will be central themes, with developments targeting technical textiles, medical products, fine-gauge fabrics and high-performance industrial materials. Knitting In circular knitting, Groz-Beckert will highlight its LCmax energy-saving needles, featuring a wave-shaped shank geometry designed to reduce friction and energy consumption while maintaining knitting performance and ease of handling. © Groz-Beckert For flat knitting, the company will introduce two special-application needles. The SAN TT has been developed for producing particularly tight loops, making it suitable for technical and medical textiles, while the new SAN FY is designed to process uneven effect yarns without compromising fabric appearance. A collaboration with Chinese company Sinotex will demonstrate fine-gauge knitting capabilities through a jointly developed knitted collar. Using the spring-loaded latch needle Vosa Spec. 89.50-45 G016, the application illustrates how finer fabrics and tighter stitch structures can be achieved for premium collars and sweater components. © Groz-Beckert The legwear segment will feature Groz-Beckert’s durable dur needles for sock and fine hosiery machines, where precision and resistance to mechanical loading are essential. © Groz-Beckert In warp knitting, the company will present its patented compound needle Spec. 51/43.36 G 101 for fine-gauge

summary: Stronger industry-academia collaboration is essential to overcome mounting operational challenges in the ready-made garment (RMG) sector of Bangladesh. Rising worker wages and energy price instability...
content: Stronger industry-academia collaboration is essential to overcome mounting operational challenges in the ready-made garment (RMG) sector of Bangladesh. Rising worker wages and energy price instability currently threaten factory operations across the country. Academic figures and corporate leaders shared these insights at a panel discussion titled "Prospects and Challenges of the RMG Sector of Bangladesh" on November 1, 2026. The Department of Textile Engineering at Green University of Bangladesh (GUB) organized the event as part of TEX-FEST 2026 at its Purbachal American City campus. Figure: Academic figures and corporate leaders shared these insights at a panel discussion titled "Prospects and Challenges of RMG Sector of Bangladesh" on November 1, 2026. The garment sector serves as the primary driver of Bangladesh's national economy. However, unaligned policies and economic pressures put continuous stress on manufacturers. Prof. Dr. Mohammad Shorif Uddin, Vice-Chancellor, Green University of Bangladesh attended the program as the chief guest. He emphasized deeper partnerships between academic institutions and apparel manufacturers to drive industrial productivity. Economic instability creates massive operational hurdles for local factories. Prof. Dr. Khawza Iftekhar Uddin Ahmed, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Green University of Bangladesh compared the RMG sector to a golden goose supporting the national economy. He warned that rising operational expenses, energy supply disruptions, and policy misalignment could severely damage the industry. He called for immediate university-industry synergy to protect the long-term sustainability of the sector. Severe energy supply shortages directly impact industrial production output. title: Gartex Texprocess expands to Eastern India with the launch of Kolkata edition in January 2027
summary: Building on nearly a decade of industry engagement and successful editions in Delhi and Mumbai, Gartex Texprocess India is set to expand its footprint to Eastern India with the launch… The post Gartex Texprocess expands to Eastern India with the launch of Kolkata edition in January 2027 appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: Building on nearly a decade of industry engagement and successful editions in Delhi and Mumbai, Gartex Texprocess India is set to expand its footprint to Eastern India with the launch of its Kolkata edition from 22–24 January 2027 at Biswa Bangla Mela Prangan, Kolkata. Organised by Messe Frankfurt Trade Fairs India Pvt Ltd and MEX Exhibitions Pvt Ltd, the Kolkata edition marks the next phase in the show’s growth journey, taking its established platform for textile and garment manufacturing to a region deeply rooted in India’s textile heritage and increasingly positioned for future manufacturing growth. West Bengal has long held a distinctive place in India’s textile landscape, with its rich handloom traditions, jute industry and established hosiery and garment manufacturing base. The state’s renowned weaving and craft clusters, including Fulia, Santipur, Bishnupur and Murshidabad, reflect a textile heritage that continues to shape the region’s identity. Kolkata and its surrounding districts are also regarded as the historical home of India’s hosiery industry, with a cluster that has grown over more than a century. The city is also a major centre for ethnic wear, kidswear, zari and embroidery work, while the Hooghly belt remains the heartland of India’s jute industry, now moving into bags, home textiles, geotextiles and composites. As the garment sector grows, so does the need for woven fabric, and the state has been encouraging powerloom and processing investment, among them the integrated textile park at Ashoknagar–Banipur. At the same time, manufacturers across Eastern India are increasingly looking towards modernisation, advanced machinery, technology adoption, capacity expansion and wider market access. summary: Key insights Bangladesh merchandise exports rose 6 percent year-on-year to $17.04 billion in July-October FY27. RMG exports increased 6.03 percent to $13.71 billion, maintaining their dominant positi...
content: Key insights Bangladesh merchandise exports rose 6 percent year-on-year to $17.04 billion in July-October FY27. RMG exports increased 6.03 percent to $13.71 billion, maintaining their dominant position in the export basket. Knitwear exports grew 7 percent to $7.71 billion, while woven garment exports increased 4.8 percent to $6.00 billion. Figure:Knitwear exports increased by 7 percent to $7.71 billion, while woven garment exports rose 4.8 percent to $6.00 billion. Bangladesh merchandise exports maintained year-on-year growth during the first four months of FY2026-27. Export earnings increased by 6 percent to $17.04 billion in July-October, compared with $16.08 billion in the same period of FY2025-26, according to Bangladesh Bank data released on November 1, 2026. RMG remains the main export engine Table 1. Bangladesh RMG export performance in July-October Category July-October FY26 (USD billion) July-October FY27 (USD billion) Growth (YoY) Knitwear 7.21 7.71 +7.0% Woven garments 5.73 6.00 +4.8% Total RMG 12.93 13.71 +6.03% Source: Bangladesh Bank; growth rates as reported. Figures are rounded. The RMG sector accounted for approximately 80.46 percent of Bangladesh's total merchandise export earnings in July-October FY27. RMG exports reached $13.71 billion, up 6.03 percent from $12.93 billion a year earlier. Within the sector, knitwear exports increased by 7 percent to $7.71 billion, while woven garment exports rose 4.8 percent to $6.00 billion. Together, the two garment segments contributed approximately 81 percent of the overall increase in merchandise export earnings during the four months. title: Bangladesh Apparel Roadshow held in Hong Kong
summary: Bangladesh’s apparel industry took centre stage in Hong Kong on 28 October, as the Bangladesh Apparel Roadshow 2026 brought together around 130+ global buyers, sourcing professionals and industry leaders to showcase Bangladesh’s manufacturing capabilities and explore opportunities for growth. Co-hosted by BGMEA and HSBC, in collaboration with the Consulate General of the People’s Republic of […] The post Bangladesh Apparel Roadshow held in Hong Kong appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Bangladesh’s apparel industry took centre stage in Hong Kong on 28 October, as the Bangladesh Apparel Roadshow 2026 brought together around 130+ global buyers, sourcing professionals and industry leaders to showcase Bangladesh’s manufacturing capabilities and explore opportunities for growth. Co-hosted by BGMEA and HSBC, in collaboration with the Consulate General of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh in Hong Kong, the event showcased Bangladesh’s manufacturing strengths, growing capabilities and ambitions for the future. A live apparel apparel showcase was among the highlights, bringing the quality, creativity and craftsmanship of Made in Bangladesh to life. The event featured opening remarks from Mahmud Hasan Khan, President of BGMEA, Oliver Jones, HSBC Hong Kong’s Head of Global Network Banking, Corporate and Institutional Banking, and Dr Shah Mohammad Tanvir Monsur, Consul General of Bangladesh in Hong Kong. Dr Rubana Huq, Chairperson of Mohammadi Group, delivered the keynote address, followed by panel discussions led by Md Mahbub ur Rahman, CEO of HSBC Bangladesh, featuring Ranjan Mahtani, Founder and Chairman of Epic Group, Sunny Malhotra, Managing Director of PDS Group, Dr Henry Soo, Managing Director of DataDevelop Consulting, Kim Hellström of H&M and Surendar Singh of Kontoor Brands. Discussions explored Bangladesh’s competitive positioning, evolving global sourcing priorities, product diversification, sustainability and the opportunities to move further up the value chain. The strong participation and exchange of perspectives reaffirmed the importance of collaboration between industry stakeholders in strengthening Bangladesh’s position in global apparel supply chains. title: Groz-Beckert to present innovations across various product areas at ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026
title_ko: 그로쯔베커르트, ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026에서 다양한 제품 영역에 걸친 혁신 발표
summary: Groz-Beckert will be presenting its highlights and innovations across the various product areas – Knitting, Weaving, Nonwovens, Sewing, Tufting and Spinning – in Hall 4.1, Booth D41 at the ITMA… The post Groz-Beckert to present innovations across various product areas at ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026 appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: Groz-Beckert will be presenting its highlights and innovations across the various product areas – Knitting, Weaving, Nonwovens, Sewing, Tufting and Spinning – in Hall 4.1, Booth D41 at the ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026. Knitting In the Circular Knitting segment, the energy-saving needles take center stage – the LCmax . With their innovative, wave-shaped shank geometry, they deliver energy efficiency, reduced friction, and exceptionally easy handling – ensuring maximum performance with minimal energy consumption. In Flat Knitting, two special-application needles are in the spotlight. The SAN TT has been specially designed for knitting particularly tight loops and is ideal for use in technical and medical textiles. The new SAN FY is engineered for processing uneven effect yarns and ensures flawless fabric appearance, even with demanding materials and intricate designs. In cooperation with SINOTEX, Groz-Beckert demonstrates the production possibilities offered by its fine-gauge technology with a jointly presented knitted collar. Equipped with the spring-loaded latch needle Vosa Spec. 89.50-45 G016, the application showcases the production of finer fabrics and tighter stitch loops, making it ideal for high-quality collars and sweater components. The Legwear product group presents its exceptionally durable dur needles for use in sock and fine hosiery machines, where the highest levels of precision and load resistance are required. In the Warp Knitting segment, Groz-Beckert presents the patented compound needle Spec. 51/43.36 G 101 for fine-gauge elastic fabrics. The reinforced plastic part provides enhanced stability, while minimal tolerances support the production of uniform, high-quality fabrics with excellent knitting performance. title: ZDHC finds strong chemical data tracking, but weaker supplier follow-up
summary: The number of fashion and textile brands achieving the highest level of sustainable chemical management under the Zero Discharge of Hazardous Chemicals (ZDHC) program increased to 21 in 2026 from 15 i...
content: The number of fashion and textile brands achieving the highest level of sustainable chemical management under the Zero Discharge of Hazardous Chemicals (ZDHC) program increased to 21 in 2026 from 15 in the previous assessment. However, the latest report shows that brands still need to do more to help suppliers solve chemical management problems. Figure: The ZDHC Gateway provides factory-level information on chemical inventory conformance and wastewater performance.Courtesy: Collected The 2026 Brands to Zero Report, independently assessed by KPMG Netherlands, examines how brands manage chemicals through company policies, purchasing practices and supply chains. The program classifies brands into three levels: Pioneer, Accelerator and Champion. More brands collect and monitor chemical data The report shows that more brands are asking their suppliers to provide chemical inventory data. The share requiring suppliers to submit ZDHC InCheck data increased from 75% to 91%. The share of brands monitoring this data also rose from 87% to 91%. ZDHC InCheck helps factories check the chemicals in their inventories against the Manufacturing Restricted Substances List (MRSL). The list sets requirements for chemical formulations used in textile, leather and footwear manufacturing. However, collecting and checking data does not always lead to action. Only 74% of brands follow up with suppliers on the findings, although this figure increased from 60% in the previous assessment. This means that some brands identify chemical management problems but do not consistently follow up to ensure that suppliers address them. ZDHC says brands should help suppliers correct problems, monitor progress and ensure that improvements continue. Chemical management should also be part of purchasing decisions

title: Fluoro-alternative finish from Dow
title_ko: Dow의 불소 대체 마감재
summary: Dow has launched a new silicone-organic hybrid textile finishing technology designed to provide durable water repellency alongside resistance to oil-based contaminants, without relying on conventional fluorinated chemistry. The new Dowsil IE-5619 DWOR Emulsion has been developed to help textile manufacturers and brands respond to increasingly stringent restrictions on fluorinated substances, while maintaining the performance, comfort […] The post Fluoro-alternative finish from Dow appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Dow has launched a new silicone-organic hybrid textile finishing technology designed to provide durable water repellency alongside resistance to oil-based contaminants, without relying on conventional fluorinated chemistry. The new Dowsil IE-5619 DWOR Emulsion has been developed to help textile manufacturers and brands respond to increasingly stringent restrictions on fluorinated substances, while maintaining the performance, comfort and appearance of finished fabrics. Achieving effective oil repellency has traditionally been one of the major challenges in developing alternatives to fluorinated textile finishes. Dow says its third-generation silicone-organic hybrid technology is designed to address this limitation, offering resistance to both water-based stains and a range of oil-based contaminants. The product is intended for use on natural, synthetic and blended fabrics, although performance must be validated for individual fabric types and finishing formulations. The new emulsion can help protect against contaminants including cooking oils, motor oil and sebum, as well as common water-based stains such as coffee, wine and milk. “For years, achieving meaningful oil repellency in textiles typically required fluorinated chemistries, which are now facing increasing restrictions,” said Juan Carlos Medina, global strategic marketing director at Dow. “Dowsil IE-5619 helps close that gap with a silicone-based, fluoro-alternative solution that delivers durable water and oil repellency while preserving the softness, breathability and aesthetics consumers expect.” The new formulation is a 30% solids concentrate designed for integration into conventional textile finishing processes. content: China and India are among the world’s most important textile manufacturing markets and have been key destinations for Swiss textile machinery for decades. Their industrial structures, raw material bases and market dynamics, however, differ considerably. These differences create distinct requirements and opportunities for Swiss suppliers of machinery, components and services. With ITMA Asia + CITME in Shanghai and India ITME in Greater Noida, two major Asian textile machinery exhibitions will take place towards the end of 2026. “China and India are both key markets for our industry, but their industrial environments differ notably,” explains Cornelia Buchwalder, secretary general of Swiss Textile Machinery. “The structure of textile production, the availability of raw materials and the importance of domestic demand all influence their investment priorities. Understanding these differences is essential for our member companies to offer technologies that meet the specific requirements of each market.” Extensive value chain China is by far the world’s largest textile manufacturing country, with an extensive and highly integrated value chain covering virtually every stage of textile production. It is also the world’s leading exporter of textiles and apparel, while its substantial domestic market generates significant additional demand. Its position in man-made fibres is particularly strong, with chemical fibre production reaching approximately 87 million tons in 2025. At the same time, China remains a major cotton producer and processor. Exports continue to play a central role in the Chinese textile industry. Chinese textile machinery manufacturers have also made considerable technological progress, creating an increasingly competitive environment for international suppliers

title: Replay: Closing Fashion’s AI Trust Gap
summary: Fashion has no compunctions about adopting AI, but confidence in its outputs has yet to catch up. Replay our live debate from last month, featuring executives from VibeIQ, Bamboo Rose and Voxelo. The post Replay: Closing Fashion’s AI Trust Gap appeared first on The Interline .
content: Fashion’s next looming AI challenge has nothing to do with uptake. In the survey portion of The Interline’s AI Report 2026 , we found that only around a quarter of respondents trusted AI’s output enough to base critical decisions on top of, and we identified a prevailing concern amongst practitioners that companies (and especially innovation leaders) are overestimating the capabilities of artificial intelligence and the extent of automation. It’s clear from the data that fashion’s spending on AI is set to keep rising, but access to the technology is evidently not the same thing as establishing trust – either in its standalone capabilities, or in its place at the heart of brands’, retailers’ and makers’ technology estates. On 15th October 2026, The Interline brought together three executives to examine that gap across product and line creation, strategic sourcing and production, and consumer-facing content. Hosted by Ben Hanson, our Editor-in-Chief, the conversation featured: Brian Lindauer , CEO of VibeIQ . Rupert Schiessl , Chief Strategy & AI Officer at Bamboo Rose . Vlad Mulhem , CEO and Co-Founder of Voxelo . The speakers all had their own different conclusions about how AI is set to change the work, and the working environment, of fashion, and each of them also fielded audience questions. Now, the replay of that live session is available to watch for the entire audience, along with a full transcript below. title: Wage issue in RMG sector: An alternative proposition
summary: Minimum wage enhancement in Bangladesh’s Ready-Made Garment (RMG) sector is economically and socially justified. Rising prices of essential commodities, housing, healthcare, and transportation, couple...
content: Minimum wage enhancement in Bangladesh’s Ready-Made Garment (RMG) sector is economically and socially justified. Rising prices of essential commodities, housing, healthcare, and transportation, coupled with inflation and BDT depreciation, continue to erode workers’ purchasing power. Therefore, nominal wage increases alone cannot ensure improved living standards. A sustainable solution requires coordinated reforms balancing workers’ welfare, industrial competitiveness, and productivity rather than relying solely on periodic wage revisions. Alternative and sustainable solutions Decentralization of factories: Encourage new RMG investments outside Dhaka through improved infrastructure, energy, transport, housing, and targeted incentives. This would reduce living costs, ease pressure on Dhaka, and promote regional development. Regional minimum wages: Introduce a transparent wage structure reflecting regional living costs, particularly housing, food, and transportation, while protecting workers’ basic living standards and ensuring equal pay for comparable work. Minimum wage benchmark in USD: Consider announcing an internationally comparable USD wage benchmark alongside legally guaranteed BDT payments. A transparent conversion mechanism and periodic review should address exchange-rate fluctuations and improve international wage comparisons. Inflation control: Strengthen market monitoring, control artificial price increases, improve supply chains, and stabilize essential commodity prices. Periodic cost-of-living adjustments should protect workers’ real purchasing power. Productivity and fair buyer pricing: Invest in workers’ skills, mid-level management, technology, and production efficiency. title_ko: Fulgar는 bio-based 섬유 논쟁을 발전시킵니다.
summary: Italian yarn manufacturer Fulgar has highlighted the potential of bio-based synthetic fibres to reduce the textile industry’s dependence on fossil resources, while emphasising the need for greater transparency, reliable certification and competitive pricing to support their wider adoption. The company contributed to an international discussion on the future of biosynthetics at the recent Performance Days […] The post Fulgar advances bio-based fibre debate appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Italian yarn manufacturer Fulgar has highlighted the potential of bio-based synthetic fibres to reduce the textile industry’s dependence on fossil resources, while emphasising the need for greater transparency, reliable certification and competitive pricing to support their wider adoption. The company contributed to an international discussion on the future of biosynthetics at the recent Performance Days exhibition in Munich, Germany, where Daniela Antunes, Fulgar’s Marketing Manager, joined industry experts to examine the opportunities and challenges associated with renewable raw materials. The panel discussion, entitled From Fossil to Vegetal: The Promises and Challenges of Biosynthetics , brought together representatives from Fulgar, Indorama Ventures, ISCC PLUS and Noosa. Moderated by Sophie Bramel, Technical Editor at Sportstextiles, the session explored the technical, environmental and commercial considerations influencing the development and adoption of biopolymers in textile applications. Central to Fulgar’s contribution was its ongoing research into next-generation polyamide yarns, particularly EVO and Q-GEO, two developments designed to combine renewable raw materials with the performance characteristics required by contemporary textile markets. EVO is a 100% bio-based yarn developed and manufactured by Fulgar using renewable feedstocks derived equally from castor oil and industrial corn. The castor oil originates from crops cultivated in arid regions that do not compete with food production, while the corn component comes from industrial crops not intended for human consumption. title_ko: Autoneum, 6,400만 유로에 Trèves Group 인수
summary: Swiss automotive supplier Autoneum is to acquire the French Trèves Group in a deal that will significantly expand its global manufacturing operations and strengthen its position in automotive acoustic and thermal insulation, interior trim and luggage compartment solutions. The acquisition will bring together two established suppliers to the international automotive industry, creating a business with […] The post Autoneum to acquire Trèves Group in €64 million deal appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Swiss automotive supplier Autoneum is to acquire the French Trèves Group in a deal that will significantly expand its global manufacturing operations and strengthen its position in automotive acoustic and thermal insulation, interior trim and luggage compartment solutions. The acquisition will bring together two established suppliers to the international automotive industry, creating a business with combined annual revenues expected to exceed CHF 2.9 billion (€3.1 billion) in 2026. Trèves, which generated revenues of approximately €720 million in 2025, employs around 4,600 people across 26 production facilities in 15 countries in Europe, North and South America, Asia and Africa. The company has longstanding relationships with major automotive manufacturers and specialises in acoustic and thermal management systems and interior components. Under the agreement announced on November 2nd, Autoneum will pay approximately €40 million upfront, with a further performance-related payment of up to €24 million possible depending on improvements in profitability and the achievement of synergies by 2029. More than 80% of the initial consideration will be settled through newly issued Autoneum shares, with approximately €7.5 million paid in cash. The shares will be subject to a three-year lock-up period. The transaction is expected to be completed in early 2027, subject to consultation with the relevant employee representative bodies and customary regulatory approvals. The planned takeover follows Autoneum’s €117 million acquisition of the automotive business of Germany’s Borgers Group in April 2023. title: Luxury Brands Know Their Buyers. Do They Know Their Customers?
summary: Product authentication has been luxury's primary use case for blockchain, but so far it's focused on visibility at the point of sale or resale. A tech founder argues it has a deeper role to play. The post Luxury Brands Know Their Buyers. Do They Know Their Customers? appeared first on The Interline .
content: Luxury brands have become remarkably good at understanding the people who buy their products. Sophisticated CRM systems, loyalty programs, and digital analytics give them a precise picture of purchasing behaviours, spending patterns, and customer preferences. Brands and maisons know, in exacting detail, who their best clients are, what they buy, how often they shop, and what they are likely to want next. They use this to put some of the world’s most sophisticated clienteling operations into practice, for the planet’s most discerning shoppers. What they have comparatively little visibility into is what happens to the products they buy after the point of sale, and the extended lives those products (which are uniquely designed for longevity, timeless style, and are seen as a store of value) now live. Products perceived as perennially stylish and valuable now no longer just get passed from one generation to the next: they circulate through resale platforms, auction houses, consignment boutiques, and private collectors, creating a second life that most brands cannot see until the item comes back into their ecosystem for service, repair, or authentication. That secondary market is no longer a fringe economy alongside luxury retail; st’s part of the system, and also part of the buying decision matrix for a growing cohort of luxury shoppers who purchase goods with the intention of parting with them afterwards. For an expanding group of consumers, the secondary market is also where their relationship with luxury begins. A first-time buyer may enter the category through a pre-owned handbag, rather than the traditional route of a gateway product like a scarf, a belt, or a fragrance. content: Heimtextil 2027 will introduce the Functional Futures Lab, a showcase of innovative materials for architecture, interior design and hospitality. The exhibition will feature experimental prototypes and commercially available solutions with applications in temperature regulation, acoustic comfort, flame protection and healthier indoor environments. Figure: Heimtextil 2027 to feature bio-based composites and next-generation textiles The Functional Futures Lab will explore material innovation through three themes: Circular Systems, Living Nature and Natural Performance. These themes will examine material origins, processing methods, durability, and functional properties. Featured innovations will include upholstery materials made from untreated wool fibers, living root systems designed to provide flame protection without toxic chemicals, durable bio-based composites, and dyes derived from food waste for textiles and wood. These materials highlight opportunities to develop alternatives to conventional raw materials and improve the functional performance of interior products. Their commercial potential will depend on production costs, scalability, durability, and compliance with relevant safety requirements. The showcase will present both early-stage research and market-ready solutions. Information on each material's development stage, including Technology Readiness Levels, will help visitors assess its readiness for practical applications. This approach will help textile manufacturers, designers, architects and hospitality professionals evaluate materials for residential and commercial projects. The Chemnitz-based company, part of the Santoni China Group, will present a 38-inch diameter, E20 gauge machine […] The post Terrot targets premium mattress fabrics appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: German circular knitting machinery manufacturer Terrot Textilmaschinen will highlight its UCC 672-ME double-electronic jacquard machine at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026 in Shanghai, China, from 20-24 November, demonstrating its capabilities for premium mattress ticking, upholstery and technical textiles. The Chemnitz-based company, part of the Santoni China Group, will present a 38-inch diameter, E20 gauge machine equipped with 88 feeders at stand H4.1 C39. The exhibition configuration will feature a specialised mattress fabric incorporating cooling yarns, differentiated comfort zones and knitted structures designed to promote ventilation on both surfaces. UCC 672-ME The UCC 672-ME features independently programmable three-way needle selection on both cylinder and dial, allowing manufacturers to control knit, tuck and miss actions at every feeder. This enables intricate jacquard patterns, three-dimensional textures, ventilation zones and reversible structures without the limitations of conventional mechanical patterning systems. Terrot UCC 672-ME knitting head. © Terrot Textilmaschinen GmbH For mattress applications, the technology allows different surface characteristics to be incorporated into a single fabric, combining supportive constructions with comfort-oriented designs. Actual cooling and breathability properties depend on yarn selection, fabric engineering and finishing. The machine also supports upholstery textiles, spacer fabrics, footwear uppers and selected outerwear applications. Available in diameters from 34 to 42 inches, the UCC 672-ME offers configurations with 88 feeders at 38 inches and 100 feeders at 42 inches. title: ITET Bangladesh urges government action to restore stability in textile and RMG industry
title_ko: ITET Bangladesh는 섬유 및 RMG 산업의 안정성을 회복하기 위한 정부 조치를 촉구합니다.
summary: The Institution of Textile Engineers and Technologists (ITET) Bangladesh has called for urgent government action to restore stability and strengthen industrial security amid rising labour unrest in th...
content: The Institution of Textile Engineers and Technologists (ITET) Bangladesh has called for urgent government action to restore stability and strengthen industrial security amid rising labour unrest in the textile and RMG sector. The organization stressed the need for uninterrupted production to safeguard Bangladesh’s key export industry and maintain investor confidence. In a statement, ITET Bangladesh expressed deep concern over recent incidents of arson, vandalism, labour unrest, protests and road blockades in different industrial areas, saying these incidents have severely disrupted normal factory operations and production. The organization noted that many factories have already shut down, raising concerns over the country's economy, employment and export trade. According to ITET Bangladesh, the industry was attempting to recover from prolonged gas crises and other challenges when the fresh wave of instability created further uncertainty about its future. It also warned that continued unrest could undermine the confidence of international buyers and investors and damage Bangladesh's image in the global market. Emphasizing the importance of protecting workers' legitimate rights and demands, ITET Bangladesh said factory security, a stable production environment and the rule of law must also be ensured. The organization called for resolving the underlying causes of labour unrest through dialogue between workers and factory owners. It also urged the authorities to conduct impartial investigations to identify those involved in arson, vandalism, looting and sabotage and bring them to justice. content: From November 20 to 24, 2026, Groz-Beckert will be presenting its highlights and innovations across the various product areas – Knitting, Weaving, Nonwovens, Sewing, Tufting and Spinning – in Hall 4.1, Booth D41 at ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026. Knitting In the Circular Knitting segment, the energy-saving needles take center stage – the LCmax™. With their innovative, wave-shaped shank geometry, they deliver energy efficiency, reduced friction, and exceptionally easy handling – ensuring maximum performance with minimal energy consumption. In Flat Knitting, two special-application needles are in the spotlight. The SAN™ TT has been specially designed for knitting particularly tight loops and is ideal for use in technical and medical textiles. The new SAN™ FY is engineered for processing uneven effect yarns and ensures flawless fabric appearance, even with demanding materials and intricate designs. In cooperation with SINOTEX, Groz-Beckert demonstrates the production possibilities offered by its fine-gauge technology with a jointly presented knitted collar. Equipped with the spring-loaded latch needle Vosa Spec. 89.50-45 G016, the application showcases the production of finer fabrics and tighter stitch loops, making it ideal for high-quality collars and sweater components. The Legwear product group presents its exceptionally durable dur™ needles for use in sock and fine hosiery machines, where the highest levels of precision and load resistance are required. In the Warp Knitting segment, Groz-Beckert presents the patented compound needle Spec. 51/43.36 G 101 for fine-gauge elastic fabrics. title: Government announces new wage board for garment workers
summary: On November 1, the Bangladesh government has formed a new wage board to determine revised minimum wages for readymade garment (RMG) workers amid ongoing labor unrest and demands for a monthly minimum...
content: On November 1, the Bangladesh government has formed a new wage board to determine revised minimum wages for readymade garment (RMG) workers amid ongoing labor unrest and demands for a monthly minimum wage of Tk 30,000. The six-member board, constituted under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, is chaired by Sheikh Ashfaqur Rahman, a senior district and sessions judge. The board includes five members representing employers, workers and the independent category. Prof. Mosleh Uddin Ahmed of the Department of Public Administration at the University of Dhaka has been appointed as the independent member. Employer representatives include Asif Ayub, Joint Secretary-General of the Bangladesh Employers’ Federation, and A.B.M. Shamsuddin, Director of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA). Worker representatives are Anwar Hossain, President of Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal, and Babul Akhter, General Secretary of the Bangladesh Garments and Industrial Workers Federation. The appointments were announced through separate notifications issued under the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006, as amended in 2026. The chairman has been instructed to initiate the process of fixing the minimum wage in consultation with all stakeholders. Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury announced the formation of the board, stating that it has been tasked with recommending a revised wage structure within six months. The review comes three years after the last wage revision in 2023, when the minimum monthly wage for garment workers was set at Tk 12,500. summary: The Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX) hosted ‘Texverse 2.0’, an inter-university textile innovation and research competition, on October 30. Organized by the BUTEX Science Club, the day-long e...
content: The Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX) hosted ‘Texverse 2.0’, an inter-university textile innovation and research competition, on October 30. Organized by the BUTEX Science Club, the day-long event brought together students from more than 25 public and private universities and textile colleges across Bangladesh. The event began at 8:00 am and featured eight competition categories: Maths Olympiad, Treasure Hunt, Quizard, Poster Presentation, Case Competition, AI Video Making, Article Writing and Project Exhibition. Students participated to showcase their knowledge, creativity, research capabilities and innovative ideas. A major highlight of the event was the official launch of KINKLE 2.0 , the club's second annual magazine. Professor Dr. Engr. Md. Zulhash Uddin, Vice-Chancellor of BUTEX, inaugurated the publication. The magazine aims to provide a platform for scientific thinking, research-based writing, innovative ideas and students' creative work. At the closing ceremony, Professor Dr. Engr. Md. Zulhash Uddin attended as the chief guest, while Engineer Md. title: Global fuel prices forecast to rise 32% in 2026 amid geopolitical tensions: World Bank
summary: Key Insights Fuel prices are forecast to rise 32% in 2026. Brent crude may average $91/barrel, up from $69 in 2025. Further conflict could push Brent to $105/barrel in 2027. Global food prices may ri...
content: Key Insights Fuel prices are forecast to rise 32% in 2026. Brent crude may average $91/barrel, up from $69 in 2025. Further conflict could push Brent to $105/barrel in 2027. Global food prices may rise 18% over 2026–27. Supply disruptions could worsen global inflation and food insecurity. Global fuel prices are projected to rise by 32% in 2026, driven by escalating conflicts in the Middle East, the Russia-Ukraine war and supply disruptions, according to the World Bank’s October 2026 Commodity Markets Outlook. The report forecasts that overall commodity prices will increase by an average of 23% this year, with energy costs accounting for a significant share of the rise. Brent crude oil is expected to average $91 per barrel in 2026, up from $69 in 2025. However, prices are projected to ease to $79 per barrel in 2027 if geopolitical tensions subside and supply conditions improve. The World Bank said the conflict in the Middle East has delivered a major shock to global energy supplies. Declining oil inventories have increased the risk that further disruptions could intensify supply shortages and push prices higher. The Russia-Ukraine war has added to market pressure by disrupting energy and food supplies. Restrictions on Russia’s refined petroleum production and exports, alongside interruptions to grain shipments through the Black Sea, have further increased uncertainty in global commodity markets. Despite the expected decline in overall commodity prices in 2027, the outlook remains vulnerable to further escalation in the Middle East. Meanwhile, the World Bank warned that, under a more adverse scenario, Brent crude could average $105 per barrel in 2027, significantly above its baseline forecast of $79. title: Global oil prices surge high in six-month
summary: On 30 October, Global crude oil prices surged more than 2%, reaching their highest levels in six months as concerns over a possible escalation of the Iran conflict heightened fears of supply disruptio...
content: On 30 October, Global crude oil prices surged more than 2%, reaching their highest levels in six months as concerns over a possible escalation of the Iran conflict heightened fears of supply disruptions. Investors are increasingly worried that the conflict could worsen following the US midterm elections, raising uncertainty over global oil supplies. Brent crude futures for December delivery settled at $117.64 per barrel on 30 October, up 2.4% from the previous session. During the trading session, prices briefly climbed above $118 per barrel. Figure: Investors are increasingly worried that the conflict could worsen following the US midterm elections, raising uncertainty over global oil supplies. Meanwhile, US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 2.1% to settle at $104.12 per barrel. Oil prices also recorded strong gains throughout October. Brent crude increased by 13.6% during the month, while WTI rose 15.2%, reflecting growing concerns over geopolitical risks and potential supply disruptions. Tensions surrounding oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz have further intensified market concerns. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) reported four incidents involving supertankers within a single day. According to the IRGC, two tankers were damaged by mines while travelling through routes prohibited by Iranian authorities. The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important energy shipping routes, handling a significant volume of global crude oil and fuel transportation. Any conflict or security threat in the waterway could disrupt shipments and put further pressure on international oil supplies. The conference brought together local and international academics, researchers, industry leaders and professionals to explore research-driven approaches to sustainability, technological advancement and industrial competitiveness in the textile and apparel sector. Addressing the conference as Chief Guest, Prof. Dr. Mamun Ahmed emphasised the need to connect academic research with real manufacturing challenges, arguing that the country's textile and apparel industry must move beyond its traditional manufacturing strengths through research, technology adoption and higher-value production. title: Bangladesh apparel industry draws global investment for clean energy transition
summary: Key Insights Bangladesh RMG sector faces a $4.8 billion funding gap to meet 2030 climate goals. Australian clean energy delegations explore battery storage partnerships to stabilize factory power. De...
content: Key Insights Bangladesh RMG sector faces a $4.8 billion funding gap to meet 2030 climate goals. Australian clean energy delegations explore battery storage partnerships to stabilize factory power. Denmark and Sweden support a 500 MW offshore wind project off Cox's Bazar. Natural gas shortages and LNG spot prices near $30 per MMBtu raise operational costs. Rooftop solar cannot power wet processing, requiring heat recovery and electrification. Bangladesh's ready-made garment industry is partnering with global fashion brands, renewable energy companies, and international development partners to adopt solar power, offshore wind, battery storage, and energy-efficient machinery. Manufacturers are making this shift to handle high energy costs, gas shortages, and strict carbon reduction demands from international buyers. However, realizing this green transition requires substantial capital expenditure. According to LightCastle Partners, Bangladesh's RMG sector requires $6.6 billion between 2025 and 2029 to achieve a 50 percent reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030. With only $1.6 billion in funding secured to date, the sector faces a massive $4.8 billion financing gap that demands urgent expansion of international climate finance, soft loans, and concessionary funding mechanisms. To bridge the financial shortfall and accelerate on-site clean energy, international solar investments and technology transfers are expanding rapidly across Bangladesh's apparel sector. Denmark's Heartland and fashion giant BESTSELLER are funding solar decarbonization models through a partnership with local cleantech venture SOLshare. title: Garment workers resume protests in Gazipur demanding Tk30,000 minimum wage
summary: Garment workers staged fresh protests in several areas of Gazipur on Sunday, demanding an increase in the minimum monthly wage to Tk30,000. The demonstrations and road blockades brought traffic on the...
content: Garment workers staged fresh protests in several areas of Gazipur on Sunday, demanding an increase in the minimum monthly wage to Tk30,000. The demonstrations and road blockades brought traffic on the Dhaka–Tangail Highway to a standstill, while protesters set fire to a police box in Konabari. Five platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel have been deployed to maintain law and order amid the unrest. On the morning of 01 November, workers took to the streets in Safipur Bazar, Chandra Palli Bidyut, Mouchak and Telichala areas of Kaliakair upazila, staging demonstrations and chanting slogans demanding higher wages. According to Kaliakair Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Shahidul Islam, workers had occupied the highway since morning, disrupting traffic on the busy route. Gazipur Deputy Commissioner Md. Nurul Karim Bhuiyan said five platoons of BGB personnel had been deployed in view of the situation. The number could be increased if necessary. In Konabari, agitated workers set fire to a police box located in the middle of the highway. They reportedly removed items from the police box and set those on fire as well, said Konabari Police Station OC Iftekhar Hossain. The protests come after nearly two weeks of demonstrations by garment workers in different parts of Gazipur over wage increases. On 31 October, workers blocked the highway around Chandra Palli Bidyut and Gate No. 3 of the Ansar Academy in Kaliakair until around 8:30 pm. Police later dispersed them using tear gas and batons. Traffic returned to normal after nearly five hours. summary: Danish garment maker Spectre has inaugurated a new green factory in Hung Yen Province, northern Vietnam, expanding its manufacturing footprint in the country while helping reduce greenhouse gas emissions through energy-efficient production, according to the Danish Embassy in Vietnam. The new facility, Spectre Hung Yen 2, opened at Song Tra Industrial Park in Thai Binh […] The post Danish garment firm Spectre opens $30mn green factory in northern Vietnam appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Danish garment maker Spectre has inaugurated a new green factory in Hung Yen Province, northern Vietnam, expanding its manufacturing footprint in the country while helping reduce greenhouse gas emissions through energy-efficient production, according to the Danish Embassy in Vietnam. The new facility, Spectre Hung Yen 2, opened at Song Tra Industrial Park in Thai Binh Ward on Friday, marking the company’s fourth factory in Vietnam and second in Hung Yen. With nearly 80 years of experience in the garment industry, Spectre specializes in producing functional apparel for premium sportswear and outdoor brands. Backed by an investment of US$30 million, the new factory is expected to cut carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 1,600 metric tons annually compared with conventional factories of a similar size. It has received LEED Gold certification, the third-highest certification level under the Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) rating system developed by the U.S. Green Building Council. The facility combines solar power with modern design solutions to improve energy efficiency and reduce its environmental footprint. It is also equipped with advanced machinery and technologies, including automation and artificial intelligence (AI) solutions, to improve production efficiency and establish higher standards across Spectre’s manufacturing operations. The factory is expected to create jobs for around 3,000 local workers. Jesper Klausen, Spectre’s co-owner and chief business development officer, said the company, was proud of its latest investment in Hung Yen. title: 12 European countries to release 42.6mn barrels of oil from strategic reserves
summary: Twelve European countries have announced plans to release 42.6 million barrels of oil from their strategic reserves by the end of January 2027 to ease concerns over global energy supplies. The release...
content: Twelve European countries have announced plans to release 42.6 million barrels of oil from their strategic reserves by the end of January 2027 to ease concerns over global energy supplies. The release will include approximately 20.5 million barrels of diesel, accounting for nearly half of the total volume. The announcement was made in a joint statement on 29 October. EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen told reporters that member states had reaffirmed their commitment to rapidly releasing the oil reserves over the coming months, with a significant portion allocated to diesel. Courtesy: Collected The participating countries are France, Germany, Italy, Belgium, Denmark, Greece, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal and Sweden. The initiative is part of an agreement reached among G7 countries earlier this month. A few weeks before the latest announcement, G7 economies had announced plans to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil to stabilize global supplies. The International Energy Agency (IEA) had also urged its member countries in mid-October to increase oil supplies from strategic reserves ahead of the winter season. All 12 countries participating in the latest initiative are IEA members. The move comes amid a sharp rise in global energy prices following the war involving the United States, Israel and Iran. The conflict has increased pressure on energy costs across Europe and the United States, raising concerns among consumers and policymakers. High energy prices have also become a significant political issue for the Trump administration ahead of next week's US congressional elections.
